purpose: What the pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti already contain, layer by layer, from reviewed library audits (research/blueprint/audit). Generated by scripts/merge_library_audit.py; do not edit by hand.

targets.target: Proper-flat coherent cohomology and cohomology-and-base-change beyond curves (finite presentation, Tor-amplitude, flatness hypotheses)
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines only absolute cohomology H^i(X, M) of an O_X-module (Ext from the constant sheaf, with long exact and Mayer-Vietoris sequences) and Mathlib has pushforward/pullback of O_X-modules. There are no higher direct images, finiteness for proper morphisms, base-change maps, semicontinuity, Tor-amplitude or perfect complexes, although the README assumes relative coherent cohomology is supplied by the existing portfolio.

targets.target: Relative degree-zero Picard functor and its representability criteria (algebraic space, effectivity)
targets.note: Only the Picard group of a commutative ring (Mathlib) and invertible sheaves with their isomorphism-class group on a single scheme (Tau Ceti) exist. There is no relative Picard functor, no sheafification of it, no Pic^0 and no representability statement.

targets.target: Artin's representability criterion itself (statement and proof)
targets.note: No Artin representability theorem exists, and there are no algebraic spaces or algebraic stacks to state it for.

targets.target: Artin input: limit preservation
targets.note: Mathlib proves that Hom_S(-, X) sends cofiltered limits of qcqs S-schemes with affine transition maps to colimits when X is locally of finite presentation (Stacks 01ZC), and gives Noetherian models of smooth algebras (Algebra.Smooth.exists_finiteType, not in declarations.tsv: public modifier). Limit preservation for moduli functors or stacks (e.g. the Picard functor) is neither formulated nor proved.

targets.target: Artin input: representable diagonal
targets.note: Mathlib defines relatively representable morphisms and proves the diagonal of an object is relatively representable iff every map from a representable is (for a full functor preserving binary products and pullbacks), which covers set-valued functors. Missing: the stack version via Isom sheaves and its verification for the Picard functor or PEL moduli.

targets.target: Artin input: deformation and obstruction functors/theories
targets.note: Only the dual-number/derivation dictionary for lifts of algebra maps (Tau Ceti) and formal smoothness (Mathlib) exist; there are no deformation categories, tangent-obstruction theories or obstruction spaces.

targets.target: Artin input: openness of versality
targets.note: No notion of versal object or versality locus exists in either library.

targets.target: Artin input: algebraization/effectivity of formal objects
targets.note: Only adic completions of rings and modules are available; there are no formal schemes, no Grothendieck existence theorem and no effectivity statements.

targets.target: Verification of the Artin inputs in every PEL application
targets.note: Application-level obligation; nothing exists because neither the PEL moduli functors nor the criterion are formalized.

targets.target: Analytification of étale presentations and descent of local-isomorphism comparisons
targets.note: Neither library has complex-analytic spaces or an analytification functor for schemes; Tau Ceti's analytic geometry is non-archimedean (adic spaces).

targets.target: Finite normalization under excellence
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the relative normalization of a qcqs morphism and proves finiteness of the integral closure of an integrally closed Noetherian domain in a finite separable extension; Tau Ceti adds the purely inseparable case over a polynomial ring over a field and Krull-Akizuki (Noetherian, not finite). Missing: excellent/Nagata (Japanese) rings and the theorem that the normalization of a reduced excellent scheme is finite.

duplicates.note: Also plans proper-flat finitely presented pushforward, flat base change, cohomology and base change and semicontinuity, the base-change package this layer extends beyond curves.
Also plans coherent pushforward under proper morphisms over locally Noetherian bases with the full cohomology-and-base-change theorem, Grauert's theorem and semicontinuity.
Also plans the fppf relative Picard functor, its rigidification, Pic^0 and representability (for curves), overlapping the relative Picard representability criteria.
States the construction of the relative degree-zero Picard functor as an algebraic space, the same object whose representability this layer is to construct.
Restates 'extend analytification to the étale presentations' and the descent of local-isomorphism comparisons for its generic-fibre moduli space.
Also lists normalization under the applicable excellence hypotheses as an internal proof task.
Also descends the analytic comparison through étale presentations of algebraic spaces with their analytification.

targets.target: Projective bundles P(E) with invertible-quotient universal property
targets.note: Mathlib builds Proj of an N-graded ring as a scheme over Spec A_0 with basic-open affine charts, functoriality (Proj.map), separatedness and (unnamed instance) properness when A is of finite type over A_0, plus maps X -> Proj A from ring maps into global sections whose irrelevant ideal generates; Tau Ceti grades Sym(M). Missing: relative Proj / P(E) over a non-affine base, the universal property via invertible quotients of E, and a named P^n_S.

targets.target: Grassmannians with universal quotient, representability and base-change laws
targets.note: Mathlib defines G(k, M; R) as submodules with finite projective quotient of constant rank k, and the functor A -> G(k, A ⊗ M; A) on R-algebras with base-change maps. Missing (listed as TODO in the file): affine charts, representability by a scheme, the universal quotient sheaf, and Grassmannians of quasi-coherent sheaves over a general base.

targets.target: Flag schemes with universal filtrations
targets.note: No flag functor or flag scheme exists; Mathlib's Flag and Module.Basis.flag are order-theoretic chains of submodules, not parameter spaces.

targets.target: Universal sheaves (O(1), universal quotients/subbundles) and base-change laws
targets.note: There are no Serre twisting sheaves O(n) on Proj, no universal quotient on a Grassmannian and no base-change isomorphism for Proj; only pointwise base-change maps of the Grassmannian functor exist.

targets.target: Relative ampleness and very ampleness
targets.note: Neither library defines ample or very ample invertible sheaves, or projective/quasi-projective morphisms; Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves and their class group only.

targets.target: Hilbert polynomials
targets.note: Mathlib's hilbertPoly p d is the polynomial eventually computing the coefficients of p/(1-X)^d over a characteristic-zero field, and Tau Ceti has a truncated Euler characteristic of cohomology over a field. Missing: Hilbert-Serre for finitely generated graded modules (a Mathlib TODO) and the Hilbert polynomial n -> chi(F(n)) of a coherent sheaf on a projective scheme.

targets.target: Boundedness statements in the Noetherian setting
targets.note: No Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, Serre vanishing, global generation or boundedness-of-families results exist.

targets.target: Closedness of the equations defining invariant subbundles and Frobenius-stable lattices
targets.note: Only isocrystals over the fraction field of Witt vectors exist; there are no closed-subscheme statements for invariant subbundles or Frobenius-stable lattices.

targets.target: Required checks: projective space as line quotients; a rank-one Grassmannian
targets.note: Module.Grassmannian with k = 1 is the functor of rank-one locally free quotients, but its identification with Proj of a polynomial ring (projective space) is not proved.

duplicates.note: Constructs the relative Grassmannian scheme of locally free rank-N quotients with affine charts, gluing and universal property.
Also plans relative ampleness, projective morphisms and relative Proj of a finitely generated graded quasi-coherent algebra.
Also plans relative Proj, the construction underlying projective bundles.

targets.target: Hilbert functor and Hilbert scheme with fixed Hilbert polynomial (representability)
targets.note: There is no Hilbert functor of flat closed subschemes and no Hilbert scheme; only the Zariski-local representability criterion (Stacks 01JJ) and the numerical Hilbert polynomial are available.

targets.target: Quot functor and Quot scheme (representability)
targets.note: No Quot functor exists; the Grassmannian functor of locally free quotients of a module over an affine base is the only quotient-parameter functor, and it is not shown to be representable.

targets.target: Properness/projectivity of H -> S and Q -> S
targets.note: Proper morphisms, the valuative criterion and properness of Proj over Spec A_0 exist, but there is no parameter space to apply them to and no notion of projective morphism.

targets.target: Base-change compatibility of Hilbert and Quot schemes
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Flatness of the universal family U -> H and of the universal quotient (distinct from flatness of H -> S)
targets.note: Flat morphisms of schemes exist, but there are no universal families.

targets.target: Relative Hom schemes and Isom schemes
targets.note: No Hom or Isom functors of schemes over a base and no representability results for them exist.

targets.target: Dual-number degree-one Hilbert example proved by the rank-one quotient criterion
targets.note: The rank-one input is in Mathlib: a finite flat morphism is an isomorphism iff its rank is constantly 1, and a finite flat module over a local ring is free (which rules out flatness of k over k[ε]); Tau Ceti computes Ext^n over dual numbers. The degree-one Hilbert functor, its representation by X and the non-flatness of X -> S are not stated.

targets.target: Boundedness and realisation inside a Grassmannian (chart equations, universal quotient, flattening locus, gluing)
targets.note: Generic gluing tools exist (Zariski-local representability, relative gluing over locally directed covers, openness of the free locus of a finitely presented module), but there is no flattening stratification, generic flatness, Grassmannian chart or boundedness argument.

targets.target: Noetherian Chow lemma: proper surjective modification by a scheme quasi-projective over the base; projective dominating scheme over a field
targets.note: Proper morphisms and birational equivalence (isomorphic dense opens) exist; quasi-projective schemes and Chow's lemma do not.

targets.target: Coherent descent/dévissage statements for the selected proper-GAGA proof
targets.note: Finitely presented and quasi-coherent sheaves exist, but there is no coherent dévissage (filtrations with integral-subscheme quotients) and no GAGA-type statement.

duplicates.note: Constructs representable Hom functors (the finite locally free Weil-restriction case) and their base change, overlapping the relative Hom schemes of this layer.
Restates the Chow-lemma and coherent dévissage/descent route to proper GAGA that this layer is to supply.

targets.target: Étale equivalence relations and their quotients (algebraic spaces)
targets.note: Mathlib has internal equivalence relations in a category, the big étale topology and relatively representable morphisms; Tau Ceti has fppf quotient sheaves of affine groups by closed normal subgroups, with representability shown only for G/G^0 over an algebraically closed field. No algebraic spaces and no quotients of schemes by étale equivalence relations exist.

targets.target: Morphisms, fibre products and properties of algebraic spaces
targets.note: Only the presheaf-level transport of a scheme morphism property to representable morphisms exists (MorphismProperty.relative); nothing specific to algebraic spaces.

targets.target: Comparison with the finite étale quotient construction of #81
targets.note: Neither library contains the #81 quotient construction (no quotient of a scheme by a finite group, no modular-curve quotient); Mathlib only has the category of finite étale algebras.

targets.target: Effective descent for (quasi-coherent) sheaves
targets.note: Mathlib proves that extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic (affine faithfully flat descent for modules) and provides descent data, IsStack and the pseudofunctor of O_X-modules; Tau Ceti has Galois descent for semilinear representations. Missing: the stack property of quasi-coherent sheaves on schemes for fpqc/fppf/étale covers.

targets.target: Effective descent for finite flat group schemes
targets.note: Descent of morphisms is available: the fpqc topology is subcanonical (unnamed instance), faithfully flat surjections of affine schemes are regular epimorphisms, and points of an affine group scheme form an fppf sheaf. Missing: effectiveness of descent data for affine or finite locally free (group) schemes.

targets.target: Effective descent for polarisations and projective objects
targets.note: Mathlib descends properties of morphisms (isomorphism, open immersion, universally closed/open/injective, smooth, étale, finite presentation) along fpqc covers, but there is no descent of ample line bundles, polarisations or projective schemes.

targets.target: Descent of a line bundle kept separate from descent of an object equipped with that line bundle
targets.note: Invertible sheaves exist on a single scheme, but there is no descent statement for them or for pairs (object, line bundle).

targets.target: Weil restriction as an algebraic space for finite locally free bases (Stacks 05YC base-change map, 05YF representability)
targets.note: No Weil restriction (restriction of scalars) functor for schemes or algebraic spaces exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Also plans effective fpqc/fppf descent and algebraic-space quotients with representable diagonals.
Constructs quotients by finite locally free equivalence relations and free finite group actions, the scheme case of the equivalence-relation quotients here.
Proves effective faithfully flat descent for affine and finite locally free schemes, polarised projective curves, group objects and level structures, overlapping the effective-descent targets.
Owns Weil restriction of affine finite-type schemes along finite locally free maps, overlapping the Weil-restriction target in this layer's handoff.
Also constructs finite-locally-free Weil restriction for affine finitely presented schemes.

targets.target: Categories fibred in groupoids
targets.note: Mathlib has (pre)fibered categories in the sense of SGA 1 VI, the bicategory of based categories, fibre categories and the Grothendieck construction. Missing: the fibred-in-groupoids condition and its API (2-fibre products, 2-Yoneda).

targets.target: Stacks over a site: descent of morphisms and effectiveness of descent data
targets.note: The definitions exist for pseudofunctors LocallyDiscrete C^op -> Cat (fibres need not be groupoids), with a characterization via covering families of a precoverage. No comparison with fibered categories and no stack instances for schemes are proved.

targets.target: Stackification
targets.note: Only sheafification of presheaves exists; there is no stackification of prestacks or fibered categories.

targets.target: Representable diagonals
targets.note: Mathlib's criterion (diagonal relatively representable iff all maps from representables are) covers set-valued presheaves, i.e. the algebraic-space case. Missing: representability of the diagonal for stacks via Isom sheaves.

targets.target: Smooth/étale atlases and algebraic (Artin, Deligne-Mumford) stacks
targets.note: Smooth and étale morphisms of schemes and the étale topologies exist; there are no atlases and no algebraic stacks.

targets.target: Quotient stacks and their algebraicity
targets.note: There are no group actions on schemes, quotient stacks or stacks of torsors; Tau Ceti's fppf quotient sheaves of affine groups by normal subgroups are the closest construction.

targets.target: Algebraicity of moduli stacks of generalised elliptic curves and polarised abelian schemes
targets.note: Only abelian varieties over a field (Tau Ceti) and Weierstrass curves (Mathlib) exist; generalised elliptic curves, abelian schemes over a base, polarisations and their moduli stacks do not.

targets.target: Deligne-Mumford, separated, proper and tame properties of stacks with distinct proofs
targets.note: Only the scheme versions of separated and proper exist; there are no Deligne-Mumford or tameness conditions.

targets.target: Existence of coarse spaces for the finite-inertia/quotient presentations used
targets.note: Mathlib shows a ring is integral over its invariants under a finite group and that the group acts transitively on the primes over a given prime (the ring-level input for Spec(B)/G). There are no coarse moduli spaces, Keel-Mori theorem or quotient schemes.

targets.target: Base-change statements for coarse spaces
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Adding or removing auxiliary prime-to-characteristic level and rigidification of automorphisms
targets.note: Tau Ceti computes Aut(E) = {±1} for a Weierstrass curve over a field with j not 0 or 1728; there are no level structures, no Serre rigidity lemma and no rigidified moduli problems.

targets.target: Normalisation
targets.note: Relative normalization of Y in X for a qcqs morphism X -> Y, with the universal property among integral factorizations, compatibility with coproducts and (unnamed IsIso instance, Stacks 03GV) smooth base change. Finiteness of the normalization is not included (see A0-extension).

targets.target: Schematic closure (scheme-theoretic image)
targets.note: Scheme-theoretic image as the closed subscheme of the kernel ideal sheaf, the factorization through it and the kernel/subscheme adjunction (full names AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.image, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toImage, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kerAdjunction; declarations.tsv records the short names). Flat base change is only shown for quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dominant morphisms.

targets.target: Descent of finite correspondences
targets.note: No correspondences on schemes (e.g. Hecke correspondences) and no descent statements for them exist.

targets.target: Required examples: finite constant-group quotient in tame characteristic and a non-tame example
targets.note: Only ring-level invariant theory exists; there are no quotient schemes by finite constant groups and no tameness notion.

targets.target: Required example: the coarse j-line and the moduli stack of elliptic curves are not interchangeable
targets.note: Mathlib shows that over a separably closed field curves with equal j are isomorphic and every j occurs, and Tau Ceti computes generic automorphism groups; neither the j-line as a coarse space nor the stack of elliptic curves exists.

There are no deformation functors on Artinian local algebras, no Schlessinger criterion, no pro-representability and no completed local rings of schemes.

targets.target: Stabilisers, versal groupoids and versality
targets.note: No versal deformations, deformation groupoids or stabiliser comparisons exist.

targets.target: Algebraisation statements (effectivity, Grothendieck existence) needed by R10/R13
targets.note: There are no formal schemes, no formal GAGA or Grothendieck existence theorem, and no effectivity results.

targets.note: None of the roadmap's parameter spaces exist, so no universal properties can be exported; affine space's universal property is the only representing-object statement of this kind in Mathlib.

targets.target: Artin representability with its hypotheses and a proof
targets.note: As in A0-extension, only generic inputs exist (limit preservation of functors of points of locally finitely presented schemes, the representable-diagonal criterion for presheaves); the theorem itself is absent.

targets.target: Embedded resolution of singularities for varieties over a characteristic-zero field by blowing up (Bierstone-Milman Theorem 11.14)
targets.note: Neither library has blowups, normal-crossings divisors or any resolution theorem; only regular local rings, smooth morphisms and the Rees algebra exist (see R09.7a-c).

targets.target: Preservation of already-resolved (regular/SNC) points (Bierstone-Milman Theorem 12.2)
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Global construction compatible with local isomorphisms (Bierstone-Milman Theorem 13.2)
targets.note: Nothing exists; no functoriality statement for resolution under étale or smooth morphisms.

targets.target: Smooth projective compactification with simple normal-crossings boundary (exported through R09.7d)
targets.note: No projective morphisms, compactifications or SNC divisors exist.

targets.target: Blowups via the Rees algebra with projective universal property and affine charts
targets.note: Mathlib's Rees algebra R[It] (a subalgebra of R[X], of finite type for finitely generated I, without a graded-ring instance) and Proj with basic-open affine charts exist, but there is no blowup scheme, exceptional divisor or universal property; the Rees algebra docstring lists blowups as future work.

targets.target: Strict, total and controlled transforms of ideals and subschemes
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.note: Nothing exists (no blowups).

targets.target: Simple normal-crossings boundary divisors and permissible smooth centres transverse to the accumulated boundary
targets.note: Cartier divisors on integral schemes (Tau Ceti), regular local rings and smooth morphisms (Mathlib) exist; there are no regular parameter systems adapted to divisors, SNC divisors or permissible centres.

targets.target: Marked ideals and their equivalence under admissible transformations
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Local order and exceptional-multiplicity calculations
targets.note: Only the order of vanishing of a rational function at a codimension-one point exists; there is no order of an ideal at a point and no multiplicity along exceptional divisors.

targets.note: Only codimension-one orders of rational functions exist; no ideal order or multiplicity invariant.

targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Isomorphism over the prescribed regular/SNC locus and the functoriality provided by the source
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Projective closure of a smooth quasi-projective variety over a characteristic-zero field
targets.note: There are no quasi-projective varieties or projective embeddings; only Proj of graded rings and general scheme-theoretic images exist.

targets.target: Smooth projective compactification with strict normal-crossings complement preserving the given smooth open
targets.note: Proper and smooth morphisms exist; compactifications and SNC complements do not.

targets.target: Analytic polydisc charts along the boundary over the complex numbers
targets.note: No complex analytification of schemes exists; Tau Ceti's polydiscs are adic (valuation-spectrum) objects, unrelated to this target.

duplicates.note: Also constructs a smooth projective compactification of nonproper smooth curves (the dimension-one case) for its logarithmic de Rham comparison.
Also constructs smooth projective completions of smooth affine complex curves by projective closure and normalization (the dimension-one case).

targets.target: Analytic structure sheaf on analytifications of finite-type complex schemes (carrier assumed from ComplexComparison PR196)
targets.note: Neither library has complex analytic spaces (singular or nonreduced), an analytification functor on schemes or the morphism X^an -> X; the PR196 carrier this layer 'uses' is not in the libraries. Closest: Mathlib turns a manifold over 𝕜 = ℂ into a locally ringed space with its sheaf of 𝕜-smooth (holomorphic) functions (smooth, reduced case only, not linked to schemes); Tau Ceti has holomorphic functions on ℂ as a sheaf of types and the Euclidean topology on complex points of affine toric schemes (no structure sheaf).

targets.target: Convergent power-series algebras ℂ{z1,...,zn} as local rings
targets.note: No ring of convergent power series or of germs of analytic functions is defined. Mathlib has analyticity predicates via formal multilinear series in any number of variables, and formal power series rings (Noetherian over a Noetherian base), but nothing convergent as a ring.

targets.target: Weierstrass preparation and division for convergent power series
targets.note: Mathlib proves Weierstrass division and preparation, with uniqueness, for one-variable formal power series A⟦X⟧ over an adically complete local ring A (hypothesis: image in the residue field nonzero). This covers formal series ℂ[[z1..zn]] but not convergent ones, since ℂ{z'} is not adically complete; the convergence estimates on polydiscs are missing.

targets.target: Noetherianity of ℂ{z} and Oka coherence of the holomorphic structure sheaf
targets.note: No coherence notion for sheaves of rings or modules exists in either library (the only 'coherent' declarations concern coherent topologies/sites and topological coherence), and no Oka theorem; only Noetherianity of formal power series.

targets.target: Coherent analytic modules via local finite presentations: independence of presentation, kernels/cokernels, tensor/Hom, restriction and gluing
targets.note: Mathlib defines locally finitely presented sheaves of modules over any sheaf of rings on a site (where SheafOfModules is abelian); Tau Ceti adds the sheafified tensor product and packages finitely presented modules on schemes. Missing: an analytic structure sheaf to apply this to, the coherence property and its closure under kernels, cokernels, tensor and internal Hom, independence of presentation, and an internal Hom sheaf of modules (Mathlib's sheafHom is a sheaf of types).

targets.target: Nonreduced closed analytic subspaces with their coherent ideal sheaves
targets.note: Only the algebraic analogue exists: quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data on schemes and the (possibly nonreduced) closed subschemes they cut out. No analytic subspaces.

targets.target: Locally free coherent analytic sheaves versus holomorphic vector bundles on smooth spaces
targets.note: Mathlib's C^n vector bundles are defined over any nontrivially normed field, so ContMDiffVectorBundle over ℂ models holomorphic vector bundles, and locally free sheaves of modules exist on any site (Tau Ceti: invertible sheaves on schemes). The sheaf of holomorphic sections and the bundle/locally-free-sheaf dictionary are absent.

targets.target: Polynomial-to-holomorphic local ring comparison O_{X,x} -> O_{X^an,x} and its faithful flatness
targets.note: No analytic local rings and no comparison map. Only general commutative algebra the proof would use: a flat local homomorphism of local rings is faithfully flat, and the adic completion of a Noetherian ring is flat.

targets.target: Analytification functor on coherent algebraic sheaves by pullback along X^an -> X, and its exactness
targets.note: The generic pullback of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed sites (left adjoint of pushforward) exists and is specialised to morphisms of schemes, but there is no morphism X^an -> X to pull back along and no exactness theorem.

targets.target: Compatibility of analytification with tensor products, internal Hom for finite presentation, duals of locally free sheaves, determinants and short exact sequences
targets.note: Tau Ceti has sheafified tensor products and exactness of forgetting module structure; internal Hom, duals and determinants of sheaves of modules are absent in both libraries, as are all compatibility isomorphisms with analytification.

targets.target: Local acyclicity and Stein-type vanishing of coherent cohomology on polydiscs and projective affine charts via analytic Cousin/∂̄ problems
targets.note: No ∂̄-operator on forms, Cousin problems, Dolbeault–Grothendieck lemma, Stein spaces or Cartan Theorem B. The sheaf-cohomology carrier the layer says to reuse exists (Mathlib Sheaf.H, defined as Ext from the constant sheaf), Tau Ceti proves flasque abelian sheaves on a space are acyclic, and Mathlib has torus integrals (the polydisc Cauchy-formula ingredient).

targets.target: Leray/Čech comparison for acyclic covers
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Čech complex functor of a family of objects, but there is no comparison map to Sheaf.H and no Leray theorem (Tau Ceti's scheme-cohomology docstring lists the Čech comparison as missing). Only the two-open Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence exists (sites in Mathlib, modules on schemes in Tau Ceti).

targets.target: Analytic twisting sheaves O(n) on complex projective space
targets.note: ℂP^n carries no topology or complex-manifold structure in the libraries (Mathlib only has the set-level equivalence OnePoint K ≃ ℙ(K²)). There is no O(n), analytic or algebraic: Mathlib has Proj of a graded ring (proper over Spec A₀ when A is of finite type over A₀) but no twisting sheaves.

targets.target: Cohomology of O(n) on ℙ^n in all degrees, with multiplication and connecting maps compared to the algebraic calculation
targets.note: Neither the analytic nor the algebraic (Serre) computation of H^i(ℙ^n, O(n)) exists, so the algebraic side of the comparison is also missing from the libraries. Related: Tau Ceti proves ℓ(n·P∞) = max(n+1, 0) on the rational function field (function-field shadow of h⁰(ℙ¹, O(n))), defines cohomology of O_X-modules on schemes, and has connecting maps and long exact sequences for Sheaf.H on any site.

targets.target: Finite-dimensionality of coherent cohomology on projective analytic spaces (Cartan–Serre)
targets.note: No finiteness theorem for sheaf cohomology, analytic or algebraic (Tau Ceti lists finite-dimensionality for proper schemes as later work). Mathlib only shows a holomorphic function on a compact preconnected complex manifold is constant (degree zero, structure sheaf).

targets.target: Generation by global sections after sufficiently high twists and finite-presentation resolutions/dévissage on projective analytic spaces
targets.note: No global generation, ampleness or Serre-twist theory in either library, analytic or algebraic (searched ample, globally generated, twisting sheaf, Serre twist).

duplicates.note: Also plans Čech H¹ of analytic sheaves by a Leray theorem for acyclic covers, acyclicity of discs from the local ∂̄-lemma and finite-dimensionality of H¹ (for compact Riemann surfaces).
Also plans the Leray and Čech-to-sheaf spectral sequences and the acyclic-basis comparison on general sites, which contain the Leray/Čech comparison for acyclic covers asked for here.

targets.target: Equivalence of coherent O_X-modules and coherent O_(X^an)-modules for a projective complex scheme (exact, fully faithful, essentially surjective), including nonreduced schemes, closed immersions and products
targets.note: Nothing analytic exists (no analytic spaces, analytification or coherent analytic sheaves; see C0), and there is no notion of projective scheme or projective morphism beyond Proj of a graded ring. The algebraic side has only the full subcategory of finitely presented O_X-modules (Tau Ceti, on Mathlib's finite-presentation condition), with no abelian-category or coherence theorems.

targets.target: Cohomology comparison H^i(X, F) ≅ H^i(X^an, F^an) in every degree, natural in F, by reduction to twists of O(n) on projective space and finite presentations
targets.note: Only the carriers exist: sheaf cohomology Sheaf.H on a site (Mathlib) and H^i(X, M) of O_X-modules on a scheme, functorial in M (Tau Ceti). There are no twisting sheaves O(n), no computation of H^i(P^n, O(n)), no finiteness theorem and no comparison map.

targets.target: Comparison of higher direct images along projective morphisms, with naturality, projection formula and base-change hypotheses
targets.note: Mathlib has the underived pushforward of O_X-modules along a morphism of schemes. Higher direct images, projective morphisms, the projection formula and cohomology and base change are absent from both libraries, algebraically as well as analytically.

targets.target: Identification of line bundles, morphisms of vector bundles, sections, coherent ideals and algebraic closed subschemes with their analytic counterparts
targets.note: The algebraic objects exist (invertible sheaves on schemes in Tau Ceti; quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data and the possibly nonreduced closed subschemes they cut out in Mathlib), and Mathlib's C^n vector bundles over ℂ model holomorphic bundles on manifolds, but there are no analytic ideal sheaves, closed analytic subspaces or comparison maps.

targets.target: Proper coherent GAGA for proper finite-type complex schemes (categorical equivalence and cohomology comparison) by Chow's lemma and coherent dévissage, without assuming projectivity
targets.note: Proper morphisms and birational equivalence of schemes exist in Mathlib, but neither the projective theorem of C2 nor the inputs of this route: there is no Chow lemma (owned by AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.2), no dévissage of coherent sheaves by integral closed subschemes and no analytic side.

targets.target: Proper algebraic spaces of finite presentation over ℂ, and descent of the comparison through étale presentations and their analytifications
targets.note: Neither library defines algebraic spaces or analytic spaces. Mathlib has only the generic tools of an étale presentation: the big étale topology on schemes and relatively representable morphisms of presheaves.

targets.target: Effective descent of coherent modules along étale presentations, algebraically and analytically, with the full-faithfulness square
targets.note: Mathlib proves effective descent of modules along a faithfully flat ring map (extension of scalars is comonadic), which covers affine étale covers, and supplies the abstract descent-data/stack formalism and the pseudofunctor of O_X-modules on schemes. Missing: the stack property of quasi-coherent or coherent sheaves on schemes and algebraic spaces for étale covers, descent of coherent analytic sheaves, and the full-faithfulness square comparing the two.

duplicates.note: Owns the Noetherian Chow lemma and the coherent dévissage/descent statements of the proper-GAGA proof, the route this layer restates.
Also plans extending analytification to étale presentations and descending local comparisons, the algebraic-space step of this layer.
Also restates extending analytification to the étale presentations of an algebraic space.

targets.target: Chow's theorem: closed analytic subspaces of complex projective space are algebraic, retaining the coherent ideal and the nonreduced structure
targets.note: There are no closed analytic subspaces, no complex-analytic projective space and no algebraization theorem; only algebraic closed subschemes cut out by quasi-coherent ideal sheaves and Proj of a graded ring (Mathlib).

targets.target: Algebraicity of holomorphic maps from proper algebraic schemes to separated finite-type targets, via an algebraic graph and the proper projection
targets.note: Proper and separated morphisms and scheme-theoretic images (the algebraic tools of the graph argument) exist in Mathlib, but there are no holomorphic maps between analytifications to algebraize.

targets.target: Full faithfulness applied to morphisms of abelian schemes, polarizations, level structures and coherent correspondences; the projective realization-to-Chow step of Baily-Borel and the GAGA step of the PEL complex comparison
targets.note: Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field with their homomorphism groups, but there are no abelian schemes over a base, polarizations, level structures or algebraic correspondences, and nothing analytic to compare them with.

targets.target: Smooth projective completion of each component of a finite-type smooth affine complex curve, by projective closure and normalization
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the relative normalization of a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism with its universal property, and the homogenization of polynomials. Missing: the projective closure of an affine curve in projective space, finiteness of the normalization, and the proof that the result is a smooth proper curve containing the affine curve as a dense open with finite complement (the regular projective model of AlgebraicCurves Layer 12 is likewise absent).

targets.target: Removing finitely many points from a connected Riemann surface preserves connectedness
targets.note: Mathlib proves that the complement of a countable set in a real vector space of dimension greater than one is connected, which is the statement on a chart ℂ ≅ ℝ², and that a charted space over a locally connected model is locally connected; Tau Ceti shows a circle minus a point is path-connected. Missing: the statement for a connected manifold modelled on ℂ, i.e. the local-to-global argument.

targets.target: Algebraic versus analytic connectedness for finite-type smooth affine complex curves, through the clopen algebraic-component decomposition and idempotents on the completed curve
targets.note: Two ingredients are in Mathlib: clopen subsets of Spec R correspond to idempotents of R, and a holomorphic function on a compact connected complex manifold is constant. The comparison itself needs analytification and projective GAGA, which are absent.

duplicates.note: Lists projective realization and Chow algebraization as steps of its own Baily–Borel proof, the same step this layer says it provides.
Also constructs smooth projective compactifications of smooth quasi-projective varieties, which covers the smooth projective completion of affine curves used here.
Constructs the regular projective model of a function field by normalizing the projective line, which is the smooth projective completion of a complex affine curve used here.
Plans the algebraization of analytic Belyi pairs over ℂ (compactification, meromorphic function field, comparison), a special case of algebraizing compact Riemann surfaces and their maps.
States the same algebraic-versus-analytic connectedness comparison for a smooth affine complex curve, as an external supplier contract.

targets.target: Algebraic de Rham complex of a smooth complex variety, built from Kähler differentials and exterior powers
targets.note: Mathlib has the Kähler differentials Ω[S⁄R] with their universal derivation, exterior powers of modules, and the presheaf of relative differentials of a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings (the general morphism-of-schemes case is a TODO in that file). Missing: the exterior derivative on the exterior powers of Ω and the de Rham complex of an algebra, its sheaf version on schemes, and its functoriality.

targets.target: Analytification of the de Rham complex and the integration/Poincaré map to the analytic resolution of the constant sheaf ℂ
targets.note: Mathlib defines the exterior derivative of differential forms on a normed space, with d ∘ d = 0 for C² forms, but there are no sheaves of holomorphic forms on analytic spaces, no holomorphic de Rham complex of sheaves and no comparison map to the constant sheaf.

targets.target: Local analytic Poincaré lemma, with naturality
targets.note: Mathlib proves the Poincaré lemma in degree one: a closed 1-form (with values in 𝕜-linear maps, 𝕜 = ℝ or ℂ) on an open convex subset of a normed space has a primitive, and a complex-differentiable function on a convex subset of ℂ has a primitive. Missing: forms of degree at least two, exactness of the holomorphic de Rham complex of sheaves on polydiscs, and naturality.

targets.target: Grothendieck's comparison of algebraic de Rham cohomology with singular cohomology with complex coefficients for proper smooth varieties, via hypercohomology, C2-C3 and the sheaf/singular comparison
targets.note: Sheaf cohomology of a single sheaf on a site (Mathlib) and singular homology, absolute (Mathlib) and relative (Tau Ceti), exist. Hypercohomology of complexes of sheaves, singular cohomology, the sheaf-versus-singular comparison assumed from ComplexComparison and the de Rham comparison itself do not.

targets.target: Compatibility with cup products, pullback, trace and the relative Gauss-Manin connection for proper smooth families
targets.note: Neither library has cup products on sheaf or singular cohomology of spaces, trace maps, relative de Rham cohomology or a Gauss-Manin connection (Tau Ceti's cup products are for continuous group cohomology).

targets.target: Smooth projective compactification and logarithmic de Rham complex of nonproper smooth curves, with the residue/localization sequence
targets.note: There are no logarithmic differentials, residue maps on schemes or compactifications of curves (see C4 for the completion). Analytically, Mathlib computes the integral of dz/(z - w) over a circle around w as 2πi, the period behind the residue of a logarithmic form.

targets.target: Regular-singular logarithmic comparison theorem and independence of the compactification
targets.note: No algebraic connections, regular singularities or logarithmic comparison theorems exist in either library.

targets.target: Compactly supported, ordinary and parabolic cohomology of open curves and their pairings
targets.note: Neither library has compactly supported or parabolic cohomology of curves or the associated duality pairings.

targets.target: Integral Betti lattices and rational coefficient structures retained before complexification
targets.note: Tau Ceti's Hodge-structure library supplies the abstract ℤ → ℚ → ℂ base-change tower (IsBaseChange models) that these lattices would use, but there is no integral Betti cohomology of varieties to carry it.

duplicates.note: Also compares algebraic de Rham cohomology, holomorphic differentials and singular cohomology, for complex elliptic curves.
Also constructs relative H¹_dR with Gauss–Manin connection and cup product and the degree-one de Rham–Betti comparison for abelian schemes.
Also distinguishes ordinary, compactly supported and parabolic cohomology of open modular curves and proves their pairings.
Also constructs smooth projective compactifications with normal-crossings boundary, of which the curve compactification here is the one-dimensional case.
Also compares Betti and de Rham realizations over embeddings into ℂ with cup-product, pushforward and trace compatibilities.
Also constructs compactly supported and parabolic cohomology with boundary maps for modular curves.
Also asks for constructed comparison maps from scheme cohomology to analytic (complex Betti) cohomology, which for de Rham cohomology is the comparison this layer builds.

targets.target: O(n) on projective space: analytic and algebraic cohomology and their comparison
targets.note: No twisting sheaves on Proj and no cohomology computation for projective space exist. The closest result is Tau Ceti's ℓ(n·P∞) = max(n + 1, 0) on the rational function field, the function-field shadow of h⁰(P¹, O(n)).

targets.target: Infinitesimal thickening of a projective point as a nonreduced test case
targets.note: Nonreduced closed subschemes can be formed from ideal sheaf data (Mathlib), but there is no analytic counterpart or comparison to test.

targets.target: Hodge line and invariant differential of a complex elliptic curve
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs the invariant differential dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) of an elliptic curve over any field as a basis of the Kähler differentials of its function field (its regularity, div ω = 0, is explicitly not proved), and Mathlib has the Weierstrass ℘-function of a lattice with ℘'² = 4℘³ - g₂℘ - g₃. Missing: the Hodge line H⁰(E, Ω¹) as coherent cohomology, the uniformization ℂ/Λ ≅ E(ℂ) and the identification of ω with dz.

targets.target: Polarized first cohomology of a complex elliptic curve
targets.note: Tau Ceti has polarized pure Hodge structures, the Riemann bilinear relations in weight one and a standard polarized weight-one structure on ℤ × ℤ, the linear algebra of H¹ of a complex torus. Missing: H¹ of an actual elliptic curve, singular or de Rham, and its identification with such a structure.

targets.target: G_m with its logarithmic residue
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs the multiplicative group scheme over any commutative ring as a group object over Spec R, and Mathlib computes the circle integral of dz/(z - w) as 2πi. Missing: the logarithmic de Rham cohomology of G_m generated by du/u, the residue map and its comparison with H¹(ℂ^×, ℂ).

targets.target: Coherent graph of an isogeny
targets.note: Tau Ceti has isogenies of Weierstrass curves as coordinate-ring pullbacks, with the pullback of the invariant differential, and Mathlib has scheme-theoretic images; the graph of an isogeny as a closed subscheme of E₁ × E₂ with its coherent ideal, and its analytic comparison, are absent.

targets.target: Comparison of f(q)dq/q with the weight-two Hodge section, keeping the relative Tate differential du/u distinct
targets.note: Mathlib defines q-expansions of functions on the upper half-plane (used by Tau Ceti for Hecke operators), but there is no Hodge bundle on modular curves, no Tate curve and no algebraic differential on a modular curve to compare with.

targets.target: Consumers receive the proved natural transformations rather than dimension equalities
targets.note: Interface requirement on the exports of C2-C5 for AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli, PELModuli, ShimuraVarieties and AutomorphicBundles; there is nothing to check until those comparisons exist.

duplicates.note: Also checks the q-expansion of f(q)dq/q against the Hodge bundle and automorphy factor, the same weight-two acceptance test.
Also compares the algebraic invariant differential, periods and Weil pairing of a complex elliptic curve with the analytic formulas.
Also identifies invariant differentials, periods and the de Rham/singular comparison of a complex elliptic curve.

targets.target: Schemes, Spec and affine schemes
targets.note: Mathlib defines schemes as locally ringed spaces locally isomorphic to Spec, with morphisms, the Spec functor and affine schemes; nothing to build.

targets.target: Sheaves of O_X-modules and quasi-coherence (M~ equivalence on affines, pullback/pushforward)
targets.note: Mathlib has the abelian category X.Modules, quasi-coherence (defined for sheaves of modules on any ringed site via local presentations), and ModuleCat R equivalent to quasi-coherent O_{Spec R}-modules. Tau Ceti adds the tensor product of O_X-modules (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorProduct) and finitely presented sheaves, which the layer does not ask for.

targets.target: Relative Spec of a quasi-coherent O_S-algebra
targets.note: Mathlib glues Spec of a 'coequifibered' presheaf of O_X-algebras on the affine Zariski site (F(D(f)) = F(U)[1/f]) into a scheme over X, and has relative Spec over an affine base (algSpec: R-algebras to schemes over Spec R); relative normalization is built this way. Missing: a named Spec functor on quasi-coherent O_S-algebras and its anti-equivalence with affine morphisms to S (Mathlib's docstring says the link to quasi-coherent algebras is still to be developed).

targets.target: Relative Proj of a graded quasi-coherent O_S-algebra
targets.note: Mathlib has Proj of an N-graded ring as a scheme over Spec A_0, with its standard affine cover, and proves Proj A -> Spec A_0 is separated, and proper when A is of finite type over A_0 (an unnamed instance in ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean). Missing: Proj of a graded quasi-coherent algebra over a general base scheme, with O(1) and base change.

targets.target: Gluing schemes along open subschemes (affine gluing)
targets.note: Mathlib glues arbitrary gluing data of schemes (not only affine pieces), with open immersions and joint surjectivity, shows a scheme is the colimit of its affine opens, and has relative gluing over a locally directed open cover of the base (Stacks 01LH).

targets.target: Fibre products of schemes
targets.note: Mathlib builds fibre products by gluing from the affine case (Spec S x_{Spec R} Spec T = Spec (S tensor_R T)); the global HasPullbacks Scheme instance is unnamed (Pullbacks.lean line 484) so it is not in the declaration list.

targets.target: Flat, smooth and etale morphisms as named morphism properties
targets.note: Defined affine-locally (flat/smooth/etale ring maps on affine opens), with stalk characterisations and Etale iff smooth of relative dimension 0 (AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.iff_smoothOfRelativeDimension_zero).

targets.target: Proper, separated and locally-of-finite-presentation morphisms as named morphism properties
targets.note: IsProper is separated + universally closed + locally of finite type; IsSeparated means the diagonal is a closed immersion. Valuative criteria are also in Mathlib (ValuativeCriterion.lean).

targets.target: Base-change and composition stability of these properties (base-change squares)
targets.note: All are MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange instances (also IsSeparated.isStableUnderBaseChange, composition instances). The acceptance remark that a flat family does not make its parameter scheme flat is a warning, not a theorem to formalise.

targets.target: fpqc and fppf topologies on schemes, subcanonical (descent of morphisms into a scheme)
targets.note: Mathlib defines the fppf and fpqc topologies on Sch and proves them subcanonical, so quasi-compact (or locally finitely presented) faithfully flat surjections are effective epimorphisms; these instances are unnamed in Sites/Fpqc.lean. Tau Ceti adds the induced fppf topology on affine R-schemes (CommAlgCat R)^op with subcanonicity.

targets.target: fpqc descent of properties of morphisms
targets.note: Isomorphisms, open immersions, surjective, universally closed/open/injective, flat, and (unnamed instances in LocalFlatDescent.lean) locally of finite type/presentation, smooth, formally unramified and etale all descend along surjective flat quasi-compact morphisms. Mathlib's Descent.lean lists descent of affine morphisms along faithfully flat maps as TODO.

targets.target: Effective fpqc/fppf descent of objects (quasi-coherent modules, affine schemes)
targets.note: Mathlib proves extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic (affine faithfully flat descent of modules in Beck form) and the Amitsur exactness R -> S => S (x)_R S; Tau Ceti proves the affine group-valued points descend. Missing: the stack statement that quasi-coherent sheaves (or affine morphisms) satisfy effective fpqc/fppf descent over schemes; Mathlib's ModuleCat/Descent.lean marks the passage to effective descent as TODO.

targets.target: Descent data, prestacks and stacks over a site (fibered categories)
targets.note: Mathlib has the general framework (pseudofunctors to Cat with descent data; stacks need not be groupoid-valued, following Giraud) and fibered categories, but no concrete geometric stack (no IsStack instance anywhere in either library).

targets.target: Representable morphisms of sheaves on Sch and representable diagonals
targets.note: Mathlib has relatively representable morphisms of presheaves, P.relative for a morphism property P, and Zariski-local representability of a sheaf on Sch (Stacks 01JJ). Missing: representability of the diagonal of a sheaf or stack and its use to define algebraic spaces/stacks.

targets.target: Algebraic spaces and algebraic-space quotients (etale equivalence relations)
targets.note: No definition of algebraic spaces or of quotients of schemes by etale/fppf equivalence relations in either library.

targets.target: Quotients by group actions with universal property and stabilizer conditions
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs, for an affine group G over a ring and a closed normal subgroup V(I), the fppf quotient sheaf G/V(I) with its universal property and torsor square, and shows G/G° is representable over an algebraically closed field. Missing: quotients of schemes or algebraic spaces by general group-scheme actions or groupoids, stabilizer group schemes, and quotient stacks [X/G].

targets.target: Algebraic (Artin/Deligne-Mumford) stacks: smooth atlas, atlas independence, separate representability and properness
targets.note: No algebraic stacks, atlases or properness of stacks in either library; only the abstract IsStack framework above exists.

targets.target: Moduli functor vs moduli stack; coarse vs fine moduli spaces
targets.note: No moduli functors, coarse or fine moduli spaces are defined in either library (Tau Ceti's universal elliptic curve and Weierstrass families are explicit families, not moduli objects).

targets.target: Zariski, etale, fppf and pro-etale sites (big and small)
targets.note: Mathlib has the big Zariski, etale, fppf/fpqc (see SF.1) and pro-etale topologies on Sch, the small etale and small pro-etale sites (pro-etale defined via weakly etale maps, following Bhatt-Scholze), and the small affine Zariski and affine etale subsites.

targets.target: Comparisons between the sites (inclusions, dense affine subsites, points), incl. cohomological comparisons
targets.note: Mathlib compares the topologies (Zariski <= etale <= pro-etale <= fpqc, fppf <= fpqc), identifies sheaves on the affine subsites, and gives a conservative family of geometric points of the small etale site. Missing: comparisons of cohomology across sites at any coefficient level (e.g. Zariski vs etale/fppf cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves, etale vs pro-etale cohomology of torsion sheaves).

targets.target: Sheaf cohomology on sites and on schemes, with long exact and Mayer-Vietoris sequences
targets.note: Mathlib defines H^n of an abelian sheaf on any site as Ext from the constant sheaf Z, with Mayer-Vietoris and a Cech complex functor (CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor, no Cech-to-derived comparison). Tau Ceti specialises to H^i(X, M) for O_X-modules with module structures, long exact sequence, Mayer-Vietoris and flasque acyclicity; Serre vanishing on affines and finiteness for proper schemes are not proved in either library.

targets.target: Etale cohomology with torsion coefficients
targets.note: Etale cohomology is available only as the general Sheaf.H applied to abelian sheaves on the small etale site (whose sheaf category Mathlib shows is Grothendieck abelian). Missing: a named etale cohomology API, constant torsion coefficient sheaves Z/n, Kummer/Artin-Schreier sequences, and any computation or finiteness result.

targets.target: l-adic and rational (Q_l) coefficients
targets.note: Mathlib defines H^i(X, Z_l) as pro-etale cohomology of the sheaf U -> C(U, Z_l) (Bhatt-Scholze 6.8.1). Missing: comparison with lim_n H^i_et(X, Z/l^n), Q_l coefficients, and constructible/lisse l-adic sheaves; Mathlib notes the comparison with the classical definition is future work.

targets.target: Localization (open-closed) sequence and extension by zero
targets.note: No extension by zero j_!, closed pushforward exact sequence 0 -> j_! j^* F -> F -> i_* i^* F -> 0 or excision/localization long exact sequence for etale sheaves in either library.

targets.target: Proper base change and smooth base change theorems
targets.note: Neither library has higher direct images for etale sheaves or base change theorems (the only 'smooth base change' in Mathlib is for normalization and integral closure).

targets.target: Compactly supported cohomology
targets.note: No Rf_! or H^i_c for schemes in either library.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves on schemes, their isomorphism classes as a commutative monoid under tensor product (inverses not asserted in general), Weil = Cartier divisors and an injective additive map Cl(X) -> line-bundle classes on Noetherian integral curves with DVR local rings; Mathlib has Pic of a commutative ring. Missing: Pic X as a group for general schemes, surjectivity of Cl(X) -> Pic(X), and the Cartier-divisor/line-bundle dictionary.

targets.target: Riemann-Roch theorem for curves (function-field form)
targets.note: Proved for an algebraic function field F/k with exact constant field (IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F): l(D) = deg D + 1 - g + l(W - D) with W the divisor of a Weil differential, deg W = 2g - 2, and the high-degree form. Stated for function fields, not for curves as schemes.

targets.target: Riemann-Roch and genus in sheaf-cohomology form on a projective curve (chi(O_X(D)) = deg D + 1 - g, g = dim H^1(X, O_X))
targets.note: Tau Ceti has H^i of O_X-modules, additivity of the truncated Euler characteristic, and the sheaf O_X(D). Missing: finite-dimensionality and vanishing of H^i on projective curves, the arithmetic genus, the cohomological Riemann-Roch theorem, and a dictionary between smooth projective curves and function fields that would transport the function-field theorem.

targets.target: Genus
targets.note: Genus of a function field defined as sup(deg D + 1 - l(D)) (a junk value if the constant field is not exact), with Riemann's inequality and dim Omega_F(0) = g. No genus of a curve as a scheme.

targets.target: Serre duality
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the repartition (adelic) duality for function fields: L(W - D) is isomorphic to Omega_F(D) and dim Omega_F(D) = i(D) (Stichtenoth 1.5.7, 1.5.14), and Kahler differentials of F/k are 1-dimensional given a separating element. Missing: sheaf-theoretic Serre duality with a dualizing sheaf on projective curves or schemes, and the identification of Weil and Kahler differentials.

targets.target: Picard schemes (representability of the relative Picard functor)
targets.note: No Picard functor or Picard scheme in either library (TauCeti.NumericalType.Pic is a purely combinatorial group attached to intersection matrices).

targets.target: Jacobian variety and Abel-Jacobi map with base point and connectedness/smoothness/projectivity hypotheses
targets.note: Tau Ceti has abelian varieties (proper geometrically integral group schemes, commutative by Mathlib's rigidity theorem) and the divisor-class shadow of Abel-Jacobi D -> [D - deg(D) x0] in abstract Pic^0 (base point of weight 1), whose fibres on effective divisors of fixed degree are complete linear systems. Missing: the Jacobian as an abelian variety and the Abel-Jacobi morphism of schemes.

targets.target: Genus zero and genus one checks
targets.note: Genus 0 with a degree-one divisor gives a rational function field; in genus one (with a degree-one divisor) degree-one places biject with Cl^0 as groups, and the points of a Weierstrass curve are the degree-zero divisor classes of its function field. That the function field of a Weierstrass curve has genus one is not stated as such.

targets.target: Extension of scalars (constant field extension) and degree behaviour
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the conorm of divisors along finite extensions of function fields (including constant field extensions) with deg Con D = n(F'/F) deg D under linear disjointness, and base change of abelian varieties. Missing: invariance of the genus under separable constant field extension and base change of Pic/Jacobians.

targets.target: k[X] is Japanese/Nagata (or its one-dimensional special case)

targets.target: normalization of k[X] in every finite extension of k(X) is a finite k[X]-module, no separability
targets.note: Present: the separable case (Mathlib, trace form; Tau Ceti's polynomial-model form) and the purely inseparable case for k[X_1..X_r] (Stacks 032O). Missing: the general mixed-separability statement (e.g. via normal closure and the purely inseparable subextension), which nobody has assembled; Krull–Akizuki gives Noetherianity only, not module-finiteness.

targets.target: R_x Noetherian, integrally closed, Krull dimension ≤ 1, fraction field F (no separability)
targets.note: Integral closedness, dimension ≤ 1 and the fraction field are separability-free Mathlib results; Noetherianity without separability is Tau Ceti's Krull–Akizuki theorem (any Noetherian domain of dimension ≤ 1, any finite extension of its fraction field), not a consequence of finite normalization as the layer prescribes (module-finiteness is not obtained).

targets.target: hence R_x is a Dedekind domain (no separability)
targets.note: Tau Ceti: the integral closure of any Dedekind domain A in any finite extension L of Frac A is Dedekind, no separability; this covers R_x (A = k[x], L = F) but no R_x-specific statement is packaged. Mathlib's criterion (Noetherian + DVR localizations; not in declarations.tsv: public modifier) is the alternative route through the places ↔ primes dictionary.

targets.target: Principal divisor hom div : Fˣ → Divisor k F, zero and pole divisors (Def. 1.4.2)

targets.target: div f = 0 iff f ∈ kˣ over an exact constant field

targets.target: Product formula: deg (f)₀ = deg (f)_∞ = [F : k(f)] and deg div f = 0 (Thm. 1.4.11)

targets.target: Cl(F), Cl⁰(F) and the degree exact sequence 0 → Cl⁰ → Cl → deg-image → 0 (Def. 1.4.3)
targets.note: Cl(F) = (Place.orderSystem hF).ClassGroup and Cl⁰ = ker degreeClass; Cl/Cl⁰ ≃ range of degree and (ker deg)/principal ≃ Cl⁰ are proved for any order system with degree-zero principal divisors (satisfied via Place.isWeightedDegreeZero_orderSystem), but are not restated under function-field names.

targets.target: Linear equivalence preserves deg and ℓ (Cor. 1.4.12(a))

targets.target: Degree-zero divisor principal iff ℓ ≥ 1 iff ℓ = 1 (Cor. 1.4.12(c))
targets.note: The ℓ = 1 form assumes IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F; the ℓ ≥ 1 form and the general ℓ = [k̃ : k] form need only hF.

targets.target: Riemann–Roch space L(D) : Submodule k F and ℓ(D) (Def. 1.4.4, Rem. 1.4.5, Def. 1.4.10)

targets.target: L(A) ≅ L(A′) for linearly equivalent divisors (Lemma 1.4.6)

targets.target: L(0) = k and L(D) = 0 when D < 0 or deg D < 0 (Lemma 1.4.7, Cor. 1.4.12(b))

targets.target: Monotonicity and dim L(D′)/L(D) ≤ deg D′ − deg D (Lemma 1.4.8)

targets.target: Finite-dimensionality of L(D) with ℓ(D) ≤ deg D⁺ + 1 (Prop. 1.4.9)

targets.target: deg D − ℓ(D) is bounded above (Prop. 1.4.14)

targets.target: elliptic F: translations form a normal subgroup ≅ Cl⁰(F) with finite quotient; Cl⁰ infinite over algebraically closed k (finite over finite k)
targets.note: Built for Weierstrass curves only ([DecidableEq F]): a faithful action of the point group on F(W) by F-automorphisms, and points ≃+ Cl⁰. Also present: equation-level Aut(E, O) = {±1} for j ∉ {0, 1728}, and finiteness of Cl⁰ over a finite constant field. Missing: normality in Aut(F/k), finiteness of the quotient, the abstract elliptic-function-field version, and infinitude of Cl⁰ over algebraically closed k.

targets.target: rigidity: an automorphism fixing 2g + 3 distinct rational places is the identity (Ex. 3.16/3.17)
targets.note: Only the totally-ramified vocabulary (Layer 6) exists. No statement about automorphisms fixing places.

targets.target: Weierstrass points (algebraically closed, char 0): generic gap sequence 1..g off a finite set, Wronskian weights with total g³ − g, weight ≤ g(g−1)/2, 2g+2 ≤ #𝒲 ≤ g³ − g, equality iff hyperelliptic, ≥ 2g+3 otherwise
targets.note: Layer 5's gap API is present: exactly g gaps at a rational place, with exact constants. No Weierstrass-point predicate, weight, function-field Wronskian or counting theorem exists. Mathlib's wronskian is the two-polynomial one used for Mason–Stothers.

targets.target: PGL₂ three-point rigidity: an element fixing ≥ 3 points of ℙ¹(k̄) is the identity
targets.note: Mathlib only records 2-pretransitivity of GL on a projectivization. No sharp 3-transitivity or fixed-point rigidity for PGL₂ was found.

targets.target: finiteness of Aut(F/k̄) for g ≥ 2 over algebraically closed char-0 k (non-hyperelliptic and hyperelliptic cases)
targets.note: Not found. The prerequisites (rigidity, Weierstrass-point counts, Prop. 6.2.4, PGL₂ rigidity) are also absent.

targets.target: Hurwitz bound |G| ≤ 84(g − 1) for finite G ≤ Aut(F/k̄), g ≥ 2, tame (char 0 or gcd(|G|, p) = 1)
targets.note: Not found. Riemann–Hurwitz for F/F^G is also absent from the baseline.

targets.note: No Hermitian function field or its automorphisms in either library.

targets.target: 12A: 'curve over k' := integral scheme, proper over k, of dimension 1, with the named bridge dim X = trdeg k(X)
targets.note: No curve predicate or structure on schemes, and no dimension-equals-transcendence-degree theorem for schemes, in either library. The field-side IsFunctionField ⟺ trdeg = 1 (under EssFiniteType) exists.

targets.target: 12A: ord_x : k(X)ˣ → ℤ at a regular closed (codimension-one) point via the DVR stalk
targets.note: Mathlib defines ord at codimension-one points of any locally Noetherian integral scheme, with junk 0 elsewhere and no DVR hypothesis. Tau Ceti packages it as an additive hom on k(X)ˣ and proves it surjective when the stalk is a DVR. On a 1-dimensional integral scheme the codimension-one points are the non-generic points.

targets.target: 12A: degree [κ(x) : k] of a closed point
targets.note: The residue degree of the structure morphism X ⟶ Spec k at x is [κ(x) : k] (finrank, junk 0 if infinite). Tau Ceti adds the tower law and the residue-degree-weighted divisor degree.

targets.target: 12A output: for regular X, k(X) is EssFiniteType with trdeg 1 (a function field), and closed points give places with matching residue fields and degrees
targets.note: No construction of a TauCeti.Place from a scheme point, and no finiteness or transcendence-degree statement for X.functionField. Tau Ceti has the 1-dimensional Hartogs lemma for DVR stalks, a related local input.

targets.target: 12B: X_F := normalization of ℙ¹_k in F, glued from Spec R_x and Spec R_{1/x}, with ν_F : X_F → ℙ¹_k finite and satisfying the universal property
targets.note: Mathlib has relative normalization of a qcqs morphism, universal among integral factorizations, which could express 'normalize ℙ¹_k in F'. But neither library has ℙ¹_k (or ℙⁿ) as a scheme, and finiteness of the normalization is also absent.

targets.target: 12B outputs: X_F Noetherian, integral, 1-dimensional, proper (finite ⇒ proper, ℙ¹ proper), regular (DVR local rings), k(X_F) ≃ₐ[k] F, closed points ↔ places
targets.note: The general tools exist in Mathlib: finite morphisms are proper (instance), and Proj of a finitely generated graded algebra is proper over Spec 𝒜₀ (instance after line 317). X_F itself and all its listed properties are absent.

targets.target: 12B: projectivity of X_F → Spec k (finite morphisms are projective; projective morphisms compose)
targets.note: No projective-morphism predicate was found in Mathlib or Tau Ceti AlgebraicGeometry.

targets.target: 12C: function-field functor and the anti-equivalence (extension of k-embeddings to finite dominant morphisms, identity/composition, full faithfulness, essential surjectivity, natural isomorphisms)
targets.note: Mathlib identifies S-morphisms Spec K(X) → Y with S-rational maps X ⇢ Y (Y locally of finite type, X integral). No extension of rational maps from regular curves, and no curve category or anti-equivalence.

targets.target: 12C acceptance: for W.FunctionField, isogenies ↔ scheme morphisms, with the place at O₁ restricting to the place at O₂
targets.note: Tau Ceti isogenies are coordinate-ring/function-field pullbacks sending infinity to infinity. There is no scheme-morphism side to compare them with.

targets.target: 12D: Weil divisors on a scheme (free abelian group on codimension-one points), principal divisors, linear equivalence, residue-degree-weighted degree, stated against Mathlib's cycle vocabulary
targets.note: Built for arbitrary schemes, with principal divisors for [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X] and the bridge to Mathlib's AlgebraicCycle. It is the JacobianChallenge Layer A development, not a model X_F. The class group is WeilDivisor.OrderSystem.ClassGroup of ofScheme.

targets.target: 12D: Weil divisors on X_F ≅ Divisor k F, matching degrees, principal divisors and linear equivalence, so the class groups agree with Cl(F)
targets.note: Both divisor theories are instances of Tau Ceti's WeilDivisor.OrderSystem (Place k F with ord_P; codimension-one points with Scheme.ord). The comparison therefore reduces to an ord-preserving bijection between points and places, and that bijection is absent.

targets.target: 12E (i): H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D)) ≅ L(D) under the divisor identification
targets.note: Present: 𝒪_X(D) with sections {f = 0 or ord_x f ≥ -D(x)} (codimension-one stalks DVR), H⁰ ≃ Γ, and the field-side L(D). Missing: X_F and the dictionary, so no comparison is stated.

targets.target: 12E (ii): dim H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = genus k F, equivalently h¹(𝒪(D)) = i(D) = ℓ(W − D) (χ-form RR + Serre duality ⟺ function-field RR)
targets.note: Sheaf cohomology Hⁱ(X, M) (as Ext) and the truncated Euler characteristic are defined. There is no finite-dimensionality for proper schemes, no vanishing above degree 1 on curves, no Serre duality and no cohomological genus.

targets.target: 12E (iii): dualizing sheaf ω_{X/k} corresponds to the canonical class W, with deg ω = 2g − 2
targets.note: Only the function-field canonical class (degree 2g − 2) exists. No dualizing or canonical sheaf on schemes was found.

targets.target: 12E acceptance: for genus-1 F with a rational place [0], h⁰(X_F, 𝒪(n·[0])) = n for n ≥ 1
targets.note: Only the function-field ladder ℓ(n·P) = n (rational P, genus 1, exact constants) exists. The scheme-side statement is absent.

targets.target: Integral-lattice predicate via an R-linear equivalence R tensor N = N_R restricting to i
targets.note: IsIntegralLattice packages Module.Free and Module.Finite over Z with Mathlib's IsBaseChange R for i; isIntegralLattice_iff restates it as an R-linear equivalence sending 1 tensor n to i n. Sorry-free.

targets.target: Injectivity, discreteness, spanning and equality of integral and real ranks of an integral lattice
targets.note: Discreteness is stated for a normed real space V: the range is discrete and is an IsZLattice. finiteDimensional is also proved.

targets.target: Naturality of integral lattices under integral linear maps
targets.note: A map of integral vectors extends uniquely to an R-linear map (extend, eq_extend, extend_id, extend_comp); being a lattice transfers along compatible equivalences and to products.

targets.target: IsToricCone on a Mathlib PointedCone: finite generation, lattice rationality, salience
targets.note: Structure with fields rational and salient (ConvexCone.Salient); finite generation is derived from rationality (IsToricCone.fg) rather than being a field. Only AddCommGroup N is assumed.

targets.target: Toric cones preserved by faces, products, injective integral maps and lattice equivalences
targets.note: IsToricCone.map needs an injective R-linear map compatible with an additive map of lattices; the equivalence version is an iff.

targets.target: Toric cones preserved under intersections
targets.note: Only intersections inside a fan are covered (they are faces by the fan axiom, hence toric). Missing: the intersection of two arbitrary toric cones for an integral lattice is toric; this needs Minkowski-Weyl (FG iff DualFG), which Mathlib mentions only in a docstring. Counterexamples.lean shows failure for a non-lattice map.

targets.target: Rays as one-dimensional Mathlib faces; finiteness of the ray type
targets.note: ToricRay is the subtype of PointedCone.Face with one-dimensional span; finiteness needs only finite generation of the cone. Rays of products and faces are also handled (prodSplit, faceEmbedding).

targets.target: Existence and uniqueness of the primitive generator of every ray
targets.note: Requires IsIntegralLattice i and a toric ray (primitiveGenerator takes a toric ambient cone and uses its face). Primitivity is TauCeti.IsPrimitive (some Z-functional takes the value 1).

targets.target: Naturality of rays and primitive generators under lattice equivalences
targets.note: Stated for a compatible pair of an additive equivalence of lattices and an R-linear equivalence; identity and composition laws hold up to a cast of the image cone.

targets.target: Generation of a toric cone by its primitive ray generators
targets.note: No theorem, in Mathlib or Tau Ceti, that a salient finitely generated cone is the hull of its rays or of its primitive ray generators; Mathlib's Krein-Milman is for compact convex sets.

targets.target: Regularity: IsToricCone plus an integral basis containing every primitive ray generator
targets.note: IsRegularCone extends IsToricCone with an integral basis indexed by Fin n and an injection of the rays into its indices whose basis vectors are the primitive generators.

targets.target: Regular cones are simplicial
targets.note: Mathlib defines PointedCone.IsSimplicial, but no theorem says regular cones are simplicial; Regular.lean says simpliciality 'is not proved here' and only bounds the number of rays by the rank.

targets.target: Faces and products of regular cones are regular
targets.note: Products are for the product lattice map i.prodMap i'.

targets.target: Block form of the transition matrix between two extending bases
targets.note: Ray columns are standard columns and, for compatible splittings into rays and a common complement, the matrix is [[1,B],[0,D]] with D unimodular; needs IsIntegralLattice and salience.

targets.target: Finite fans of toric cones: definition, support, completeness
targets.note: Fan carries IsIntegralLattice, a finite set of toric cones, face closure and the left half of the intersection axiom (the right half is Fan.inf_isFaceOf_right).

targets.target: Open subfans, products of fans and subdivisions
targets.note: Subfans are face-closed subsets of cones; support_prod, isComplete_prod_iff, IsRegular.prod and IsSubdivision.refl/trans/prod are also proved. There is no star-subdivision construction.

targets.target: Fan morphisms with identity, composition and support functoriality
targets.note: FanHom stores the lattice map, the real map and the cone condition; the real map is forced (FanHom.realMap_eq). Also comp_id, id_comp, prodMap, fst/snd and leastCone.

targets.target: Dual affine semigroup of integral characters nonnegative on a cone and its finite generation (Gordan)
targets.note: No dual-semigroup construction and no Gordan lemma for rational cones. Mathlib has only the equalizer version for well-quasi-ordered monoids such as N^k (Submonoid.fg_eqLocusM, whose additive form is not indexed) and the predicate IsAffineAddMonoid (Mathlib/Algebra/AffineMonoid/Basic.lean line 20; its declarations.tsv row is misparsed with name 'abbrev').

targets.target: Face localization, functoriality and regular-coordinate equivalence N^k x Z^(n-k) of dual semigroups
targets.note: Nothing about dual semigroups exists, so none of these statements is present; only the extending-basis data and the generic contravariant map on complex points of a semigroup homomorphism.

targets.target: Affine toric scheme Spec C[S_sigma], link to a ToricVariety instance, dense torus and torus action
targets.note: Neither library has AlgebraicGeometry.ToricVariety or an affine-monoid toric-variety construction (these live only in the external Toric project). Tau Ceti has the diagonalizable group scheme D(G) = Spec R[G] for finitely generated commutative groups, a candidate dense torus, but no affine toric scheme and no torus action on one.

targets.target: Face inclusions give affine open immersions with identity, composition, overlap and cocycle laws
targets.note: Mathlib proves Spec S -> Spec R is an open immersion when S is a localization of R away from one element, and R[T,T^-1] is the localization of R[X] away from X (the ray-to-zero-cone case). The toric lemma that C[S_tau] is a localization of C[S_sigma] away from a character is absent.

targets.target: Gluing the affine schemes of a finite fan; global torus, action, cone opens, algebraic toric maps and their functoriality
targets.note: Mathlib's general and locally directed gluing of diagrams of open immersions fits the face poset of a fan, but no fan scheme, global torus action or toric morphism is built.

targets.target: Effectivity HodgeStructure.IsEffective (F^0 = ⊤, equivalently F^(n+1) = ⊥)

targets.target: Weight-one instance bridge: real form V_ℝ with its structure map, the complex structure J of an effective weight-one structure, identification of its ±i-eigenspaces with H^(1,0), H^(0,1), and the converse construction from J

targets.target: Invertible sheaves (locally free rank-one O_X-modules) on a scheme, closed under tensor product
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines invertible sheaves on an arbitrary scheme as the full subcategory of X.Modules that are locally free of rank one (a site-level predicate), and proves closure under tensor product. Mathlib has only SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree.

targets.target: Picard group Pic X: isomorphism classes of line bundles as a group under tensor product
targets.note: Tau Ceti's LineBundleClass X (iso classes of invertible sheaves) is only a commutative monoid under tensor product: duals/inverses of invertible sheaves are not constructed, so no group Pic X exists. Mathlib's CommRing.Pic is the Picard group of a ring (affine case) only.

targets.target: Weil divisors: finite formal Z-sums of codimension-one points of a scheme
targets.note: Defined for every scheme as WeilDivisor on the codimension-one points, and identified with Mathlib's AlgebraicCycle X Z restricted to finite support in codimension one; Mathlib alone has only algebraic cycles, no divisor API.

targets.target: Cartier divisors and principal divisors (Cartier and Weil)
targets.note: Cartier divisors are global sections of the sheaf quotient K_X^x/O_X^x, defined only for integral schemes (enough for curves); principal Weil divisors come from Mathlib's Scheme.ord assembled by OrderSystem.ofScheme on Noetherian integral schemes.

targets.target: Weil = Cartier on a smooth curve
targets.note: Additive equivalence for Noetherian integral schemes of dimension <= 1 whose codimension-one local rings are DVRs (hypotheses as instance plus hX : forall x, coheight x <= 1); a smooth connected curve satisfies these, but no lemma deriving them from smoothness was found.

targets.target: Cartier/Weil divisors to line bundles, D -> O_X(D), and Cl(X) = Pic X
targets.note: On Noetherian integral curves with DVR local rings, O_X(D) is invertible, O_X(D+E) = O_X(D) (x) O_X(E), and Cl(X) -> line-bundle classes is an injective additive map; surjectivity (every line bundle comes from a divisor), a direct Cartier-divisor-to-line-bundle map, and Cl(X) = Pic X are missing. Affine Dedekind case: classGroupAddEquiv with Mathlib's ClassGroup, and Mathlib's ClassGroup.equivPic.

targets.target: Divisor degree sum_x [kappa(x):k] ord_x
targets.note: relativeDegree f weights coefficients by residue degrees of f : X -> Y; applied to the structure morphism of a curve over k it is the divisor degree, and D - (deg D) x0 has degree zero at a rational point.

targets.target: deg L := chi(L) - chi(O_X) for line bundles, and agreement with the divisor degree
targets.note: Only a truncated alternating sum of cohomology dimensions and its conditional additivity exist; no degree of a line bundle via Euler characteristics and no comparison with sum_x [kappa(x):k] ord_x.

targets.target: Pic^0 X = ker deg as an abstract group
targets.note: picZero is the kernel of the weighted degree on a divisor class group, but it takes as a hypothesis that principal divisors have degree zero; that hypothesis is proved only for places of an algebraic function field (product formula), not for OrderSystem.ofScheme on a proper curve, and it is on divisor classes, not on Pic X of line bundles.
