targets.target: Coherent (finitely presented) O_X-modules and their cohomology H^i(X,F), with long exact sequence and k-linear structure
targets.note: Mathlib has Ext-based cohomology of abelian sheaves on any site and SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation; Tau Ceti packages H^i(X,M) for every O_X-module (H^0 = global sections, long exact and Mayer-Vietoris sequences, Gamma(X,O_X)-module structure) and the category of finitely presented sheaves (coherent on locally Noetherian X).

targets.target: Acyclicity of affines: H^i(Spec A, quasi-coherent F) = 0 for i > 0
targets.note: Only acyclicity of flasque sheaves (hence skyscrapers) is proved; Serre vanishing for quasi-coherent sheaves on affine schemes is not, and Tau Ceti notes the missing comparison between H' on an open and cohomology of the restricted sheaf.

targets.target: Cech cohomology agrees with derived-functor cohomology on a separated scheme
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Cech complex of a presheaf for a family of objects, and Mayer-Vietoris for two opens is exact; no Cech-to-derived comparison theorem exists.

targets.target: Finite-dimensionality of H^i(X,F) for coherent F on proper X/k
targets.note: No finiteness theorem for coherent cohomology of proper schemes; the Tau Ceti Euler-characteristic results take finite-dimensionality as a hypothesis. Only the function-field analogues (L(D) and the repartition cokernel A_F/(A_F(D)+F) are finite-dimensional) exist.

targets.target: Vanishing above dimension (H^2 = 0 on a curve)
targets.note: Only conditional vanishing: if X is covered by two opens which, with their intersection, have no higher cohomology, then H^n = 0 for n >= 2. No Grothendieck vanishing and no unconditional H^2 = 0 for curves.

targets.target: Genus g := dim_k H^1(X, O_X)
targets.note: No scheme-level genus. The function-field genus (Stichtenoth: sup of deg D + 1 - l(D)) is proved to equal dim_k A_F/(A_F(0)+F), the adelic H^1(O), and the dimension of regular Weil differentials, for an algebraic function field with exact constant field; no bridge to curves as schemes.

targets.target: Riemann-Roch chi(L) = deg L + 1 - g
targets.note: Proved for divisors of an algebraic function field F/k with exact constant field: l(D) = deg D + 1 - g + l(W - D), with i(D) = dim_k A_F/(A_F(D)+F) (adelic H^1). Missing: the scheme/line-bundle statement via coherent cohomology and Euler characteristics, and the comparison of places with closed points of a curve.

targets.target: Serre duality with the relative dualizing sheaf omega_{X/k}: H^i(L) = H^{1-i}(omega (x) L^{-1})^*
targets.note: Function-field duality (Stichtenoth 1.5.14) is proved: L(W - D) = Omega_F(D), the Weil differentials, which are the dual of A_F/(A_F(D)+F). There is no dualizing sheaf or sheaf of differentials of a scheme (Mathlib has only a presheaf-of-modules relative differentials construction) and no scheme-level Serre duality.

targets.target: deg omega_{X/k} = 2g - 2
targets.note: Proved for the canonical divisor class of Weil differentials of a function field with exact constant field; nothing for the dualizing sheaf of a curve.

targets.note: No base-change comparison map or flat base change theorem for cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves in either library.

targets.note: No semicontinuity of fibre cohomology dimensions, Grauert's theorem, or cohomology-and-base-change theorem.

targets.target: Theorem on formal functions
targets.note: No formal completion of schemes along closed subschemes and no theorem on formal functions.

targets.target: Relative effective Cartier divisors
targets.note: Only Mathlib's ideal sheaves/closed subschemes exist; no effective Cartier divisors (even absolute, as closed subschemes cut out locally by a nonzerodivisor) and no relative version flat over the base.

targets.target: Symmetric powers Sym^d X as schemes (smooth projective for a smooth curve)
targets.note: Tau Ceti only has the set-level model: effective degree-d formal divisors on a type of points are equivalent to Mathlib's Sym X d. No scheme Sym^d X, no quotients of schemes by finite groups, no smoothness/projectivity.

Develops relative effective Cartier divisors on smooth relative curves (fibre criterion, sections, sums, base change, degree), the Layer C relative-divisor target.
Plans the theorem on formal functions (and formal GAGA) in the proper finite-presentation setting, a stated Layer C target.

targets.target: Relative Picard functor Pic_{X/k}: fppf sheafification of T -> Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)
targets.note: Mathlib has the fppf topology on schemes and Tau Ceti has line-bundle classes on a single scheme (monoid only); there is no pullback-functorial Pic(X_T), no quotient by Pic(T), and no Picard sheaf.

targets.target: Picard stack vs Picard functor/sheaf vs rigidified functor, and the Brauer-type obstruction between Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) and Pic_{X/k}(T)
targets.note: Only the Brauer group of a field exists as an ingredient; none of the three Picard objects and no obstruction sequence.

targets.target: Rigidification along the section x0 and the Poincare bundle
targets.note: No line bundles trivialized along a section, no rigidified Picard functor, no Poincare bundle.

targets.target: Pic^0 as the degree-0 open-and-closed component / subfunctor of degree-0 line bundles on geometric fibres, with local constancy of degree in flat families
targets.note: Only the abstract group Pic^0 of divisor classes (Layer A) exists; no functorial Pic^0, no degree on fibres of flat families, no local constancy.

targets.target: Representability via symmetric powers: Abel maps AJ_d : Sym^d X -> Pic^d, D -> O_X(D - d x0), birational and surjective for d = g
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the set-level divisor-class shadow (D -> [D - deg D x0] in abstract Pic^0, fibres on Sym X d are complete linear systems, and for function fields every degree-0 class has an effective representative once the degree is >= g); Mathlib has Zariski-local representability of sheaves. No scheme morphism, no Sym^d X, no birationality, no representability of Pic^0.

Owns the Hilbert and Quot schemes with representability, projectivity and base change, the Grothendieck route this layer states for the general Picard scheme.

targets.target: Abelian variety over k (smooth, proper, geometrically connected group scheme) with basic API and dim
targets.note: Bundled as a proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K (equivalent for group schemes over a field); smoothness and geometric connectedness are derived, and there are commutative Hom groups, End ring, finite products, zero object, base change along field extensions. dim is the topological Krull dimension; nothing computes it (e.g. dim = dim T_0 A).

targets.target: Commutativity is automatic (rigidity)
targets.note: Mathlib proves a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative; Tau Ceti installs it as an instance on AbelianVariety.

targets.target: Tangent space at the identity of an abelian variety
targets.note: T_0 A is the Zariski tangent space at the identity as a finite-dimensional K-vector space, with dimension that of m/m^2; the regular-point formula dim T_x = coheight x exists for schemes, but it is not applied to abelian varieties.

targets.target: T_0 Pic^0 = H^1(X, O_X), hence dim Jac X = g
targets.note: No Pic^0 scheme, no identification of its tangent space with H^1(X,O_X), no scheme-level genus, and no dimension computation.

targets.target: Theorem of the cube / theorem of the square
targets.note: Not present in either library (no line bundles on products of abelian varieties, no seesaw).

targets.target: Dual abelian variety
targets.note: No dual abelian variety (needs Pic^0 of an abelian variety); Tau Ceti's Cartier duality is only for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes.

targets.target: Polarizations; the theta divisor gives Jac a principal polarization
targets.note: No polarizations, no phi_L : A -> A^dual, no theta divisor.

targets.target: [n] as an isogeny
targets.note: [n] is defined in End A and isogenies (finite surjective homomorphisms, no separability assumption) are defined with base change, but only [-1] is proved to be an isogeny; [n] for n != 0 is missing. For Weierstrass elliptic curves (function-field model, not AbelianVariety) [n] is an isogeny of degree n^2.

targets.target: Characteristic p: p-torsion non-etale, inseparable isogenies, no hidden perfect-field assumptions
targets.note: The AbelianVariety isogeny notion avoids separability and perfect-field assumptions, but nothing about p-torsion or inseparable isogenies of abelian varieties is proved; only for Weierstrass elliptic curves is [n] shown separable iff n != 0 in the base field.

targets.target: Operations on quasi-coherent / finitely presented O_X-modules needed to construct Omega_{X/S}, Fitting ideals, conductors and normalization exact sequences, with pullback compatibility (Mathlib #39989)
targets.note: The predicates, tilde/affine-presentation API and pullback/pushforward functors of O_X-modules are in Mathlib, Tau Ceti packages finitely presented sheaves as a full subcategory, Mathlib has a presheaf-level universal derivation for a morphism of presheaves of rings (identity-functor case only) and the ring-theoretic conductor of R<x> in S. Missing: Omega_{X/S} as a quasi-coherent sheaf on schemes, Fitting ideals (absent from both libraries), the conductor ideal sheaf, normalization exact sequences, and preservation of quasi-coherence/finite presentation under pullback (only pushforward, open restriction and pullback of free sheaves are covered at this pin).

targets.target: Relative dimension <= d and pure relative dimension d for locally finite type morphisms, defined fibrewise via Krull dimension; isomorphism invariance, locality, arbitrary base change, composition bound <= d + e
targets.note: No fibrewise relative-dimension predicate exists; Mathlib only has relative dimension for smooth morphisms (SmoothOfRelativeDimension, with base change and composition) plus scheme-theoretic fibres and topological Krull dimension. Tau Ceti proves the affine input that dim(K tensor_k A) = dim A for a finitely generated k-algebra A and a field extension K/k, but nothing at scheme level.

targets.target: FamilyOfCurves f: proper, flat, finitely presented, relative dimension <= 1, with base-change and isomorphism API (geometric connectedness and genus kept separate)
targets.note: The constituent morphism properties and their base-change stability are in Mathlib, but the predicate is absent in both libraries because the relative-dimension bound is absent.

targets.target: Generic and special fibres over a DVR: open immersion of the generic fibre, closed immersion of the special fibre, compatibility with scalar extension, and explicit comparison of the base-change generic fibre with Scheme.Hom.fiber at the generic point via kappa(eta) = K
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines genericFiber (base change along any R -> K) and specialFiber (base change to the residue field of a local ring), proves the generic fibre is an open subscheme when R is a DVR with fraction field K, the special fibre is a closed subscheme over any local ring, the canonical isomorphism with Mathlib's fibre at the generic point for any domain R with IsFractionRing R K (with projection lemmas), and the iterated scalar-extension isomorphism for any tower R -> K -> L; Model.genericι and Model.isOpenImmersion_genericι transport this to models. No separate lemma is stated for special fibres after a DVR extension, but that follows from the general tower isomorphism.

targets.target: FiniteDVRExtension R K package (finite separable K'/K, integral closure, chosen maximal ideal above the closed point, localization, fraction-field identification, domination), finite and separable towers, and common-refinement lemmas embedding two packages compatibly into a third
targets.note: The package with its scalar towers, proofs that the chosen local ring is a DVR with fraction field K' dominating R (isLocalHom_algebraMap, under_maximalIdeal_localRing), existence for every finite separable K'/K, compatible maps (field embedding plus local map with a commuting square) forming a category, and finiteness/separability of the induced field towers (Hom.fieldFinite, Hom.fieldSeparable) are proved. Missing: common refinement; Tower.lean explicitly says the existence of a third package receiving two given ones compatibly is not asserted.

targets.target: Flat finitely presented models of C/K over R with explicit generic-fibre isomorphism: model morphisms, category instance, categorical model isomorphisms, base-change functors, separate properness predicate
targets.note: Model records the total space, a flat, locally finitely presented, quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism to Spec R and an isomorphism in Over (Spec K) from the base-change generic fibre to C; Model.Hom must respect that identification, an (anonymous) Category instance and faithful functor Model.forget exist, model isomorphisms are exactly the morphisms with invertible total-space map, and properness is a separate abbrev. Missing: base-change functors of models along DVR extensions (baseChangeHom only base-changes a morphism to the generic fibre).

targets.target: Kähler differentials and Fitting ideals developed far enough to form the relative singular closed subscheme Sing(f)
targets.note: Mathlib has algebraic Kähler differentials, the smooth locus of an essentially finite type algebra as the complement of the support of H1 of the cotangent complex intersected with the free locus of Omega, and the open smooth locus of a locally finitely presented morphism of schemes, so only the underlying closed set of Sing(f) is available. Missing: the sheaf Omega_{X/S}, Fitting ideals, and the closed-subscheme structure on Sing(f).

targets.target: Syntomic morphisms (flat, locally finitely presented local complete intersections) and their relative-dimension API
targets.note: No local complete intersection or syntomic notion exists for algebras or scheme morphisms in either library; Mathlib only has regular sequences and presentations, whose dimension docstring notes it is meaningful only for complete intersections.

targets.target: AtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f defined by syntomic of relative dimension one with Sing(f) -> S unramified, and the equivalent fibrewise condition (flat, lfp, pure one-dimensional fibres with at worst nodes)
targets.note: No node or nodal-family notion exists; only the ingredient morphism properties (flat, lfp, formally unramified) are available.

targets.target: Local normal form at a node: completed local ring kbar[[x,y]]/(xy), and étale-local charts U -> Spec R'[u,v]/(uv) or Spec R'[u,v]/(uv - pi^n) over an étale DVR extension R'/R with commuting triangles
targets.note: Absent. The only node-specific material is Tau Ceti's coordinate-level tangent quadratic of a singular Weierstrass cubic; Mathlib's étale-local structure theorem covers standard smooth algebras, not nodes.

targets.target: Smooth relative curves are nodal; nodality is stable under base change and local for the étale topology
targets.note: Absent because nodality is undefined; only base-change stability of smoothness of fixed relative dimension exists.

targets.target: Singular locus of a proper nodal curve over a field is finite étale with branch scheme finite étale of degree two; after one finite separable extension split and label nodes, branches and geometric components with the pairing involution
targets.note: Absent; Mathlib only provides a subscheme structure on an irreducible component of a Noetherian scheme.

targets.target: Normalization of a nodal curve, the conductor, and the normalization exact sequence for O_X
targets.note: Mathlib has the relative normalization of a qcqs morphism with its universal property (normalizationDesc, normalization.hom_ext) and smooth base change, plus the ring-theoretic conductor of R<x> in S. Missing: the normalization of a reduced nodal curve as a finite birational map, the conductor ideal sheaf, and the exact sequence 0 -> O_X -> nu_* O -> sum of kappa(nodes) -> 0.

targets.target: Dual graph of a proper geometric nodal curve: finite nonempty connected multigraph with loops (vertices = components of the normalization, edges = nodes), component genera, special flags, valence by half-edges, connectedness, and p_a(X) = sum g_v + b_1
targets.note: No dual graph or genus formula exists. Mathlib's Graph α β gives multigraphs with loops but no connectivity, Betti number or half-edge valence API; Tau Ceti's topologicalGenus is 1 - #vertices + #edges of the simple intersection graph of an abstract numerical type (a Layer 6 object without loops or multiple edges).

targets.target: Rational tails and rational bridges, invariance under field extension, instability iff nonpositive log-canonical degree, and iterative recomputation after contraction
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

duplicates.note: Also constructs the dual (metric) graph of the special fibre of a semistable model with vertex genera and proves that graph genus plus vertex genera recovers the curve genus, overlapping the dual-graph and p_a = sum g_v + b_1 targets.

States the normalization/nodes and dual graph of a proper strictly semistable curve over a henselian trait as its own construction (for nearby cycles), partially overlapping the normalization and dual-graph targets.

targets.target: Coherent sheaves over locally Noetherian bases, coherent proper pushforward, R^i f_*, finite-dimensionality over proper curves, vanishing above degree one, cohomology and base change, Grauert, upper semicontinuity, and R^1 f_* O_X for proper flat nodal families (contracts J-B, J-C)
targets.note: Only foundations exist: Tau Ceti defines H^i(X, M) for every O_X-module with long exact sequences, Mayer–Vietoris (H^n = 0 for n >= 2 on a two-open cover, with positive-degree acyclicity of the opens assumed), module structures over global functions and the base ring, and a truncated Euler characteristic; Mathlib has the underived pushforward of O_X-modules. Missing: coherent sheaves, R^i f_*, the finiteness and vanishing theorems, cohomology and base change, Grauert, semicontinuity and the nodal R^1 f_* O_X results.

targets.target: Arithmetic genus: definition, normalization/dual-graph formula, invariance in proper flat families, HasGenus f g via R^1 f_* O_X locally free of rank g with fibres H^1(X_sbar, O)
targets.note: No scheme-level arithmetic genus dim H^1(X, O_X) is defined; Tau Ceti has only additivity of dim H^0 - dim H^1 on short exact sequences (assuming finite-dimensionality and H^2 vanishing), the genus of a function field, and the signed genus of an abstract numerical type.

targets.target: Relative dualizing complex/sheaf for proper flat finitely presented relative Cohen–Macaulay curves; invertibility and arbitrary base change for Gorenstein fibres; nodal case via a syntomic morphism through a smooth embedding (Stacks 0E6N); agreement with the Jacobian roadmap's omega_{X/k}
targets.note: No dualizing sheaf, Cohen–Macaulay or Gorenstein notion exists in either library; the nearest material is Tau Ceti's space of Weil differentials of a function field.

targets.target: Componentwise degree formula on a geometric nodal fibre: deg(omega|_E) = 2g(E~) - 2 + #branches above nodes on E (plus markings)
targets.note: Absent: it needs the dualizing sheaf, degrees of invertible sheaves on components and normalization data, none of which exist.

targets.target: Invertible-sheaf API (tensor powers, Cartier divisors, pullback, degree on components, global generation, relative ampleness), projective morphisms and relative Proj of a finitely generated graded quasi-coherent algebra connected to Mathlib's Proj, and proper models by scheme-theoretic closure in P^N_R
targets.note: Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves with tensor products and their isomorphism classes as a commutative monoid, Cartier divisors only on integral schemes (Weil–Cartier equivalence for Noetherian integral schemes of dimension <= 1 with DVR codimension-one local rings), and locally principal Weil divisor -> invertible sheaf; Mathlib has Proj of a graded ring with an (anonymous) IsProper instance for Proj.toSpecZero and scheme-theoretic images. Missing: duals, powers and pullback of invertible sheaves, degree on components, global generation, ampleness, projective morphisms, relative Proj, P^N_R, and the closure-model construction.

targets.target: A section through the relative smooth locus is an effective Cartier divisor; sums of pairwise-disjoint such sections are effective Cartier divisors; both commute with arbitrary base change
targets.note: No effective (relative) Cartier divisor notion for closed subschemes exists; Tau Ceti's Cartier divisors are global sections of K^x/O^x on integral schemes.

targets.target: Ampleness criterion on a proper curve by positive degree on every geometric irreducible component; explicit degree bounds and global generation of omega^m and omega(sum s_i)^m
targets.note: Absent: no ampleness, global generation, degree of invertible sheaves or dualizing sheaf in either library.

targets.target: Openness of the fibrewise-ample locus of an invertible sheaf on a proper finitely presented family, identified with the relatively ample locus
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Effective étale descent for schemes with a compatible relatively ample invertible sheaf (descend the graded section algebra, recover by relative Proj), including descent of morphisms, sections, multiplication and polarization with cocycle and base-change coherence
targets.note: Mathlib proves the fpqc topology on schemes is subcanonical (anonymous instance) and that étale <= pro-étale <= fpqc (Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology, Scheme.proetaleTopology_le_fpqcTopology), so morphisms and sections descend along étale covers, and has the descent-data/stack formalism and comonadicity of extension of scalars along faithfully flat ring maps. Missing: effective descent of quasi-coherent sheaves and graded algebras on schemes (marked TODO in Mathlib), and polarized scheme descent via relative Proj.

targets.target: Contraction descent: for proper surjective c : X -> Y over S with O_Y = c_* O_X universally, S-morphisms to separated V constant on geometric fibres of c factor uniquely through Y, compatibly with base change
targets.note: Absent; only the ingredient that universally closed morphisms are closed maps is available.

targets.target: Prestable families (proper, at-worst-nodal, pure relative dimension one, geometrically connected fibres), equivalence with universal f_* O_X = O_S, restriction, pullback and fibre API
targets.note: Absent; only geometric connectedness of morphisms (Mathlib) is available as an ingredient.

targets.target: SemistableFamily and StableFamily with genus bounds; semistable iff no rational tails iff fibrewise global generation of omega^m (m >= 2); stable iff no rational tails or bridges iff omega relatively ample
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Isomorphism and automorphism groups of (pointed) families; finite abstract automorphism group and no infinitesimal automorphisms for a stable geometric fibre

targets.target: Shared scheme pushout identifying smooth sections and external clutching (two pointed prestable families of genera g1, g2 with markings I+{a}, J+{b}; genus g1 + g2, markings I+J, dual graph with one new edge, b_1 additive)
targets.note: Absent: no pushouts of schemes along closed immersions, clutching, or dual graphs in either library.

targets.target: Self-clutching (markings I+{a,b}, genus g + 1, one new edge possibly a loop), with properness, flatness, finite presentation, nodality, stability, normalization and pushout universal properties, marking-set equivalences to Fin n, reindexing naturality and base change for both constructors

targets.target: forgetLastContraction fibre analysis: B = omega(s_1 + ... + s_n) is fibrewise nef, at most one zero-degree component per geometric fibre (tail or bridge), explicit fibre contractions, and B is the pullback of the ample log-dualizing sheaf of the contracted curve
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Locally uniform global generation, H^1-vanishing and normal generation of high powers of B; locally free pushforwards with surjective evaluation/multiplication; base-change-compatible Veronese section algebra with unchanged relative Proj
targets.note: Absent; only Proj of a single graded ring exists (no relative Proj, Veronese invariance, or cohomology and base change).

targets.target: Contraction c : C -> C' to the relative Proj: C' -> S flat and finitely presented, geometric fibres equal the explicit contractions, nodality, connectedness and genus, descended pairwise-disjoint smooth sections, universal c_* O_C = O_C' and R^1 c_* O_C = 0, universal property, uniqueness and coherent base change
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Rees algebra of a quasi-coherent finite-type ideal, as a graded quasi-coherent algebra
targets.note: Mathlib has only the ring-level Rees algebra R[It] of an ideal, as an ungraded subalgebra of R[X] generated in degree one and of finite type when I is finitely generated, plus ideal sheaves on schemes. Missing: the graded-ring structure on it and the sheaf of Rees algebras of a quasi-coherent ideal.

targets.target: Blowup as relative Proj of the Rees algebra: universal property, properness/projectivity, flat base change, isomorphism away from the centre, exceptional divisor, strict transform, affine charts
targets.note: Neither library has blowups, relative Proj, exceptional divisors or strict transforms. Mathlib only has Proj of a graded ring and its properness over Spec of the degree-zero part (finite-type case), which would give properness of an affine blowup once a graded Rees algebra exists. The Tau Ceti LowDimTopology/Plumbing 'blowUp' files are combinatorial plumbing-graph moves, not scheme blowups.

targets.target: Test case Spec R[x,y]/(xy - pi^n): blowing up the singular point keeps the family nodal and lowers n by 2; termination in a regular total space
targets.note: No local nodal models or blowup computations exist. Mathlib's regular local rings (with the cotangent-space criterion) are only the ingredient for testing regularity of the total space.

targets.target: Cartier/Weil intersection multiplicities on a regular two-dimensional scheme (vertical divisors on a proper regular model over a DVR): bilinearity, projection formula, self-intersection
targets.note: No intersection numbers or pairing of divisors on surfaces exist in either library. The available ingredients are module length, orders of vanishing at codimension-one points, Tau Ceti Cartier divisors on integral schemes and the locally principal Weil-to-Cartier dictionary.

targets.target: Negative-semidefinite intersection matrix of the special-fibre components, with kernel spanned by the fibre
targets.note: The geometric statement is absent. Tau Ceti proves only the kernel half of the linear algebra (Stacks 0C5X): for a matrix over an ordered field with nonnegative off-diagonal entries, connected positive-entry graph and a positive kernel vector, every kernel vector is proportional to it. The inequality x^T A x <= 0 is not proved.

targets.target: Resolution in the required scope: a normal proper model of a smooth curve over a DVR becomes regular after finitely many normalized blowups in closed points; common resolution of two regular models; finiteness of the normalizations over a non-excellent DVR when the generic fibre is smooth
targets.note: Mathlib has relative normalization of a qcqs morphism with its universal property (and smooth base change), but no finiteness of normalization, no regular-scheme notion and no resolution statement.

targets.target: Exceptional curves of the first kind and the curve-on-surface (Castelnuovo) contraction theorem, preserving properness and the generic fibre
targets.note: Only the numerical shadow exists: a (-1)-index of an abstract numerical type (g_i = 0, a_ii = -w_i). There is no geometric exceptional-curve notion and no contraction theorem.

duplicates.note: Also plans blowups via the Rees algebra with their projective universal property, affine charts and strict/total transforms (for characteristic-zero resolution), the same construction as this layer's blowup target.

Plans arithmetic-surface resolution, local charts, vertical components and intersection multiplicities on a regular proper model of an elliptic curve, overlapping the resolution and intersection-multiplicity targets.

Plans finite-place intersection lengths on regular models of curves, vertical divisors, intersection matrices and their kernel, and projection formulas, overlapping this layer's intersection-theory target.
Lists flattening by blowup and strict transforms among its own tasks, overlapping the blowup and strict-transform target.

targets.target: Regular proper model of a smooth projective curve over a DVR, constructed from Layer 4
targets.note: Tau Ceti packages flat finitely presented models with an explicit generic-fibre identification, forming a category, with a separate properness predicate (Layer 0 material). Neither library defines regular schemes or models (Mathlib has only regular local rings and regular rings), and none is constructed.

targets.target: Relative minimality: no exceptional curve of the first kind in the special fibre
targets.note: Only the numerical analogue exists: an abstract numerical type is minimal when it has no (-1)-index. There is no geometric minimality predicate for models.

targets.target: Every regular proper model contracts to a minimal one
targets.note: No contraction theory for models exists.

targets.target: For positive generic genus, uniqueness of the minimal regular model up to unique isomorphism and its terminal mapping property among regular models
targets.note: The 'minimal models' in the libraries are minimal Weierstrass equations (maximal discriminant valuation among integral equations, with Tau Ceti comparing two of them), not minimal regular models of arithmetic surfaces.

targets.target: Components and multiplicities of the special fibre: div_X(pi) = sum m_i [C_i], and the effective Cartier subscheme cut out by pi equals X_s
targets.note: Ingredients only: principal Weil divisors on Noetherian integral schemes built from Mathlib's orders of vanishing, and principal Cartier divisors on integral schemes. Special-fibre components, their multiplicities and the divisor identity are absent.

targets.target: Intersection relations for the special-fibre components, adjunction and the genus formula
targets.note: Needs the Layer 4 intersection theory and relative dualizing sheaves, which do not exist.

targets.target: Criterion: a geometrically reduced, connected special fibre with geometrically smooth components and only ordinary nodes over the algebraic closure gives a prestable model; equivalent form using finite separable residue extensions at singular points
targets.note: Neither library has nodes, at-worst-nodal morphisms or prestable families (Layers 1 and 3).

targets.target: Genus-zero exception: minimal regular models need not be unique (e.g. the two contractions of T1 T2 - pi T0^2 = 0 in P^2_R)
targets.note: No example or statement exists.

duplicates.note: Plans a regular proper flat model of an elliptic curve over O_{F,S} together with the minimal-regular-model results and vertical components, overlapping this layer's regular and minimal model targets (for genus one over a Dedekind base).
Lists regular models of curves over number fields with their vertical divisors among its own constructions, overlapping the regular-model and special-fibre component targets.

targets.target: Abstract numerical type exactly as in Stacks 0C6Z (nonempty finite component set, m_i, w_i > 0, g_i >= 0, symmetric A with nonnegative off-diagonal entries, connected graph, sum_j a_ij m_j = 0, w_i | a_ij)
targets.note: A structure with a nonempty Fintype component type, multiplicities and weights in N+, genera in N, a Matrix.IsSymm integer intersection matrix, nonnegative off-diagonal entries, connectedness as ReflTransGen of (i != j and 0 < a_ij), the fibre relation and w_i | a_ij, matching 0C6Z field for field. Basic consequences such as a_ii < 0 when n > 1 (0C74) are proved.

targets.target: Equivalence of graph connectedness with the source's no-disconnected-cut condition
targets.note: The matrix lemma is an iff for any matrix with nonnegative off-diagonal entries over a partial order (no symmetry needed). It discharges the connected field from the Stacks cut condition; the numerical-type lemma gives the converse direction in Adj form.

targets.target: Reindexing and equivalence of numerical types
targets.note: Reindexing is along any equivalence of component types, with reindex_refl and reindex_reindex. Equiv (Stacks 0C70) has refl, symm and trans with groupoid laws, and types are equivalent exactly when one is a reindexing of the other. Genus, minimality, Pic and torsion are all shown invariant.

targets.target: Signed genus g(T) = 1 + sum m_i (w_i (g_i - 1) - a_ii/2) as an integer, with sum m_i a_ii even and the halving done once
targets.note: The value is in Z, not truncated to N, and the halving is applied once to the whole sum (Stacks 0C71/0C72). The file checks g(T) = 3 for the README's weighted example, g(T) = -1 for its genus-zero variant, and a type with odd diagonal entries.

targets.target: Numerical type of a regular model (kappa_i = H^0(C_i, O), w_i = [kappa_i : k], g_i = dim H^1(C_i, O)) and identification of g(T) with the generic-fibre genus
targets.note: Only the abstract combinatorial structure exists; nothing constructs a numerical type from a regular model or compares its genus with the generic fibre. This needs Layers 4-5 and coherent cohomology.

targets.target: Pic(T) as the cokernel of e_i -> sum_j (a_ij / w_j) e_j with exact integer division (Stacks 0C7H)
targets.note: Pic(T) is the quotient of Z^Component by the span of the rows of A' = (a_ij / w_j); exactness of the division comes from symmetry plus the row divisibility axiom. A total-degree map Pic(T) -> Z is also provided.

targets.target: Injection Pic(T) -> Coker(A) induced by e_j -> w_j e_j, not an equality (Stacks 0CE7)
targets.note: Injectivity is proved, and surjectivity holds exactly when every weight is 1. The README's worked computation for its example (Pic(T) = Z against the raw cokernel Z + Z/2, and the w = (1,2) case) is not checked in Lean.

targets.target: Rank-one finite generation of Pic(T), reindexing invariance, and prime torsion
targets.note: finrank_Z Pic(T) = 1 (Stacks 0C7I), with finite generation inherited from Z^n as an instance. Pic(T)[l] is a finite ZMod l-module of cardinality l^dim for prime l. Equivalences induce isomorphisms of Pic and of l-torsion, preserving degree, dimension and cardinality.

targets.target: Combinatorial bounds relating Pic(T)[l], the first Betti number g_top of the graph, geometric genera of components and the genus (Stacks 0C6X, 0C7C, 0C9X and the Section 55.17 inequalities)
targets.note: Present: g_top = 1 - n + e, g_top >= 0 (0C78) and the tree criterion. Missing: g >= g_top for minimal types with n > 1 (0C7C), dim Coker(A)[l] <= g_top for l coprime to all a_ij and m_i (0C6X), dim Pic(T)[l] <= g (and <= g_top for minimal T) for l > 768g (0C9X), and every inequality involving geometric genera of components.

targets.target: Classification and boundedness results for minimal numerical types used by the Artin-Winters argument (Stacks Sections 55.5-55.7)
targets.note: Present: (-1)- and (-2)-indices with the sign of genus contributions (0C75, 0C7D), g >= 1 for minimal types with n > 1 (0C7B), the neighbour bounds of 0C9U, and all four bounds of 0C9V (also genus_lt_arithmeticGenus and multiplicity_mul_abs_intersection_self_le), proved without the g >= 2 hypothesis. Missing: m_i |a_ij| <= 768g (0C9W), the classification of proper (-2)-subgraphs (55.5), the minimal types of genus 0 and 1 (0C8S, 0C8T), contraction of a (-1)-index (0C77) with its Picard map (0C7J), and Pic(T) = Z for g <= 0 (0C7K).

targets.target: Comparison of line bundles on the regular model, generic fibre, special fibre, reduced special fibre and numerical type; specialization maps and exact sequences injecting generic l-torsion into Pic of the reduced special fibre (Stacks Section 55.13)
targets.note: Only the numerical side exists (multidegrees, Pic(T), total degree, torsion). There are no models, no Picard groups of special fibres and no specialization maps.

targets.target: For a smooth projective genus-g curve and prime l != char k: a finite separable K'/K with a K'-rational point and Pic(C_K')[l] = (Z/l)^(2g), with the explicit degree bound
targets.note: Absent, as is its J-D/J-E input (Pic^0 as an abelian variety with the structure of its l-torsion). Tau Ceti has only the abstract degree-zero class group, and the nearest result is the count #ker[n] = n^2 for an elliptic curve over an algebraically closed field.

targets.target: Numerical conclusion: for g >= 2 and l > 768g, l != char k, a minimal regular model with full l-torsion has multiplicity-one, geometrically smooth components and at-worst-nodal special fibre
targets.note: Neither the geometric statement nor its numerical input (0C9W/0C9X) exists.

duplicates.note: Constructs the degree-zero Picard and generalised Jacobian of semistable curves, the toric character group from the dual graph and the component-group description related to the Neron model, overlapping the comparison of Picard groups of the special fibre with the numerical type and its torsion.

targets.target: HasNodalReduction C R: C over the fraction field of a fixed DVR has a proper at-worst-nodal model over it
targets.note: Tau Ceti has models with a generic-fibre identification and a properness predicate, but no at-worst-nodal predicate (Layer 1) and no HasNodalReduction.

targets.target: Genus zero: nodal reduction after a separable extension of degree at most 2, with C_K' isomorphic to P^1_K'
targets.note: Only a function-field ingredient exists: a genus-zero function field with a degree-one divisor is k-isomorphic to RatFunc k. Missing: the quadratic separable splitting extension, the scheme-level isomorphism with P^1, and the smooth model over the DVR.

targets.target: Genus one: nodal reduction after finite separable extension; the minimal regular model's special fibre is a smooth genus-one curve or a cycle of rational curves
targets.note: The libraries classify reduction of minimal Weierstrass equations (good, multiplicative, split multiplicative, additive) and transfer split multiplicative reduction between minimal equations. There is no potential semistable reduction theorem, no treatment of genus-one curves without a rational point, and no regular models.

targets.target: Genus g >= 2: nodal reduction via Layers 5-6 with the uniform degree bound B_g = (2g-2)(l^(2g))! for l' < l the first two primes above 768g (Stacks 0CDM)
targets.note: No statement or ingredient beyond the abstract numerical-type theory of Layer 6 exists.

targets.target: Both forms (a chosen DVR R' above R, and simultaneous nodal models at every localization of the integral closure in one extension, derived from K'-rationality of full l-torsion), plus compatibility with further finite base extension
targets.note: Only the Layer 0 packaging of a finite separable extension with a chosen place above the closed point, and maps of such packages, exist. Common refinement is explicitly not yet asserted there, and no reduction statement exists.

targets.target: Equivalence between semistable reduction of the curve and of its Jacobian under additional residue-field hypotheses
targets.note: Neither library has the Jacobian variety of a curve (Tau Ceti has only the abstract group Pic^0 of degree-zero divisor classes) or semistable reduction of abelian varieties, so this is absent.

duplicates.note: Lists semistable reduction among its own constructions (unscoped), overlapping this layer's main target, although it says stable reduction should be routed through existing owners.

Owns semistable reduction for abelian varieties after a finite extension with the monodromy criterion on the Tate module, which is the Jacobian half of this layer's curve-vs-Jacobian equivalence of semistable reduction.

targets.target: Over a field: iterated contraction of rational tails (termination by the number of geometric components, dual graph recomputed), global generation of ω^⊗2 and ω^⊗3 and the needed vanishing on the tail-free genus ≥ 2 curve, contraction of rational bridges, identification of the stable curve with Proj of the canonical ring, and characterization of the fibrewise contraction by stable target, genus, c_*𝒪 = 𝒪 and R¹c_*𝒪 = 0
targets.note: Neither library has nodal curves, dual graphs, rational tails or bridges, a dualizing sheaf, canonical rings or contraction morphisms. Mathlib only supplies Proj of a graded ring and the morphism X → Proj A induced by a ring map A → Γ(X, 𝒪_X) under which the irrelevant ideal generates the unit ideal.

targets.target: Stabilization of a prestable genus ≥ 2 family over a locally Noetherian base: étale-locally add disjoint auxiliary smooth sections making the source pointed-stable (separable smooth points on each geometric component, étale-local lifting, openness of pointed stability), then forget them one at a time with the Layer 3 single-marking contraction; termination by marking count, with geometric fibres the iterated tail-and-bridge contraction
targets.note: No prestable or pointed-stable families, no result producing étale-local sections of a smooth morphism through prescribed points, no openness of pointed stability and no single-marking contraction exist. Mathlib has only the open smooth locus of a locally finitely presented morphism.

targets.target: Uniqueness among contractions with the prescribed geometric fibres (universal c_*𝒪 = 𝒪 plus contraction descent), independence of the auxiliary sections and their order, cocycle condition on overlaps, and polarized étale descent to C → Cˢᵗ → S; the descended family is proper, flat, finitely presented and stable, and the universal c_*𝒪 and R¹c_*𝒪 statements survive descent
targets.note: Mathlib proves the fpqc and fppf topologies on schemes are subcanonical, so morphisms descend along such covers, but neither library has effective descent of (polarized) schemes, relative Proj, higher direct images R¹c_* or a contraction-descent theorem.

targets.target: Stabilization is the identity on already stable fibres and commutes coherently with arbitrary base change; for a tail-free family it is the relative Proj of the pluricanonical algebra, after proving relative generation and base change
targets.note: Only the absolute construction Proj A → Spec A₀ of a graded ring exists (Mathlib). There is no relative Proj of a quasi-coherent graded algebra, no pluricanonical algebra and no stabilization to compare with.

targets.target: Classical stable-reduction existence theorem: a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus ≥ 2 over K acquires a stable model over the local ring of a chosen place of a finite separable extension, via semistable reduction followed by stabilization
targets.note: Tau Ceti has only the Layer 0 packaging: finite separable DVR extensions with a chosen place (whose local ring is proved to be a DVR dominating R) and flat finitely presented models with an explicit generic-fibre identification. There is no semistable reduction, stable family or existence theorem.

targets.target: Uniqueness of stable models over a fixed DVR: the generic-fibre identification extends, through a common regular model and the canonical stabilization, to a unique isomorphism of models
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines model morphisms that respect the generic-fibre identification and proves that model isomorphisms are exactly the morphisms that are isomorphisms on total spaces. Regular models, stabilization and the uniqueness theorem are absent.

targets.target: Stable-reduction interface packaging existence after a finite DVR extension, uniqueness over a fixed DVR and compatibility after a common finite extension
targets.note: Chosen finite DVR extensions form a category and every finite separable extension underlies such a package, but the Tau Ceti file explicitly does not construct common refinements, and there is no stable-reduction statement to package.

targets.target: Extend the generic markings to sections of a proper model by properness, then use finite base change and blowups to make their closures pairwise disjoint and contained in the smooth locus, tracking the generic-fibre identifications
targets.note: Mathlib's valuative criteria (existence for universally closed morphisms, uniqueness for separated ones, over any valuation ring) extend each K-point of the generic fibre of a proper model to a unique section over the DVR; Tau Ceti records the pullback square of a model's chosen generic fibre. Missing: blowups (absent in both libraries) and the finite-base-change and blowup procedure making the extended sections disjoint and smooth, with the generic-fibre bookkeeping for markings.

targets.target: Pointed stabilization of a pointed prestable family with 2g − 2 + n > 0 by the auxiliary-section construction (original markings retained, descent by the final ample log-dualizing sheaf), and the geometric-fibre algorithm (delete an unmarked tail, move the marking of a one-marked tail to its attachment point, replace an unmarked bridge by a node) with termination, order independence and disjoint smooth remaining markings
targets.note: Neither library has marked or pointed curve families, a log-dualizing sheaf, dual graphs with special flags, or any contraction or stabilization construction.

targets.target: Graded log-canonical algebra with multiplication and base-change maps for each nef single-marking step and identification of its Proj with that step's contraction; the composite preserves an already stable marked generic fibre, is unique with the fibrewise contraction property and commutes coherently with base change
targets.note: Mathlib has Proj of a graded ring and its functoriality along graded ring maps, but there are no section algebras of line bundles on schemes, no relative Proj and no dualizing sheaf in either library.

targets.target: Stable pointed reduction for smooth generic curves whenever 2g − 2 + n > 0, including (g, n) = (0, n ≥ 3) and (1, n ≥ 1), after a finite separable extension, together with uniqueness over the fixed DVR
targets.note: Only the Layer 0 packaging of chosen finite DVR extensions and of models with generic-fibre identifications exists (Tau Ceti); there are no pointed stable families and no reduction theorem.

targets.target: Extension to an already stable pointed nodal generic fibre: split and label nodes, branches and components after a finite separable extension, normalize, treat paired branches as markings, apply the pointed theorem componentwise after a common extension and glue by clutching; the glued family is nodal, stable and independent of choices
targets.note: Mathlib has the relative normalization of a qcqs morphism with its universal property, but neither library has nodes, branch labelling, scheme pushouts along sections (clutching) or pointed stable reduction.

targets.target: Forgetting a marking followed by pointed stabilization, with compatibility with base change and coherence of repeated forgetting
targets.note: Absent in both libraries: there are no marked families, forgetful maps or stabilization.

targets.target: Valuative interface: essential existence after a finite DVR extension and unique extension over a fixed DVR, stated as the input for properness of M̄_{g,n} and of stable-map moduli
targets.note: Mathlib's valuative criterion is about morphisms of schemes and arbitrary valuation rings (its reduction to DVRs over a Noetherian base is listed as future work), and Tau Ceti has the finite DVR extension package; the stable-curve valuative statement itself is absent.

duplicates.note: Its internal proof task 2 (de Jong's curve fibrations) states extension of the generic curve and its marked boundary after finite base extension and stable/semistable reduction of that pointed family, to be proved there unless a stable-curve supplier with matching hypotheses exists, overlapping the pointed stable-reduction targets here.

Its contraction of Néron polygons for generalised elliptic curves is the genus-one special case of contracting rational components without markings, i.e. of the pointed stabilization constructed here.

targets.target: PrestableMap q n for a target q : V → S: a pointed prestable family π : C → S with n ordered markings and F : C → V with F ≫ q = π, projections to the source family, and pullback along S' → S through chosen pullbacks, independent of the choices up to canonical isomorphism
targets.note: Neither library has prestable or pointed curve families or any stable-map structure; only general category theory, such as uniqueness of pullbacks up to canonical isomorphism, is available.

targets.target: Isomorphisms of prestable maps over a fixed target (isomorphisms of pointed source curves commuting with F): identity, inverse, composition, extensionality, and transport along isomorphisms of base and target
targets.note: Only generic isomorphisms in over-categories exist (Mathlib); there is no groupoid of prestable maps.

targets.target: Abstract automorphism group of each geometric fibre for a separated locally finitely presented target, and infinitesimal automorphisms over an algebraically closed k (automorphisms over k[ε]/(ε²) reducing to the identity, fixing the markings and commuting with F), with the tangent space identified with the kernel of Der_k(𝒪_C) vanishing along the markings → Der(F⁻¹𝒪_V, 𝒪_C)
targets.note: The available ingredients are general or ring-level: automorphism groups of objects of a category (Mathlib), derivations as lifts to square-zero extensions (Mathlib) and to dual numbers (Tau Ceti). Neither library has derivation sheaves on schemes, automorphism groups of marked curves or maps, or the infinitesimal-automorphism computation.

targets.target: Contracted irreducible components of a geometric fibre: relate constancy of F on the component, set-theoretic image of dimension zero and, for a target with an ample invertible sheaf, degree zero of its pullback; invariance under field extension and target isomorphism
targets.note: Mathlib provides scheme-theoretic fibres and a closed-subscheme structure on irreducible components of Noetherian schemes, but neither library defines contracted components, ample sheaves or degrees of line bundles on curves.

targets.target: IsStableMap F: fibrewise positivity of the log-canonical degree (normalization genus and special flags) on every contracted geometric component; invariance under isomorphism and arbitrary base change; openness over a locally Noetherian base for projective targets with relatively ample L, via fibrewise ampleness of ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) ⊗ F^*(L^⊗3)
targets.note: No stability predicate, dualizing sheaf, ampleness notion or openness-of-ampleness theorem exists in either library.

targets.target: Automorphism criterion for separated locally finitely presented targets: F is stable iff every geometric fibre has finite automorphism group; infinitesimal automorphisms vanish under componentwise generic separability of the noncontracted components
targets.note: Absent in both libraries: there are no automorphism groups of pointed curves or maps and no finiteness or unramifiedness criterion.

targets.target: Ampleness criterion for a projective target with relatively ample L: stability iff relative ampleness of ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) ⊗ F^*(L^⊗3), independence of L, and the same for every exponent ≥ 3
targets.note: Mathlib has the pullback functor on sheaves of modules over schemes and Tau Ceti defines invertible sheaves with tensor products, but there are no tensor powers, relative dualizing sheaf, relative ampleness or projective morphisms.

targets.target: A constant prestable map is stable iff its pointed source is stable, while a nonconstant map can be stable with unstable source (an API theorem, not a field of PrestableMap)
targets.note: Absent: neither stable pointed curves nor stable maps are defined in either library.

targets.target: Evaluation morphism evᵢ = sᵢ ≫ F : S → V at the i-th marking, compatible with base change, reindexing of markings, isomorphisms of stable maps and postcomposition on the target
targets.note: Absent: neither library has stable maps or marked families, hence no evaluation morphisms.

targets.target: Polarization degree of a map and of each geometric irreducible component, deg F^*L: nonnegativity, additivity over the components of a nodal curve, invariance under algebraically closed field extension, and local constancy of total degree in connected families
targets.note: Neither library defines the degree of an invertible sheaf on a proper curve; Tau Ceti has only the residue-degree-weighted degree of scheme Weil divisors, and Mathlib the pullback of sheaves of modules. No component degrees, additivity or constancy statements exist.

targets.target: Decorated dual graph with marking legs and component degrees: genus and total-degree formulas, vertex stability (a degree-zero vertex is stable iff 2g_v − 2 + val(v) + markings(v) > 0, equivalently with + 3d_v for a polarization), valence counting half-edges so loops count twice, restriction to a component, normalization at a node and reconstruction of the numerical data
targets.note: Mathlib's multigraph Graph α β allows loops and parallel edges but has no degree, connectivity or Betti-number API; Tau Ceti's numerical-type topological genus is 1 − #components + #edges of a simple intersection graph, without loops, legs, vertex genera or degrees. No dual graph of a curve exists in either library.

targets.target: Contraction descent for proper surjective contractions of prestable curves with universally connected genus-zero fibres and c_*𝒪_C = 𝒪_{C'}: for separated V → S, a map constant on each contracted subcurve factors uniquely through the contraction, compatibly with base change
targets.note: Neither the general contraction-descent theorem of Layer 2 nor this specialization exists; Mathlib's descent of morphisms is only along fpqc and fppf covers, which contractions are not.

targets.target: Reindexing markings by equivalences and the single-marking contraction for a stable map to a projective target when 2g − 2 + n' + 3d > 0 (Behrend–Manin Prop. 3.10, Lemmas 3.11–3.12): nefness of A = ω_{C/S}(Σ retained sᵢ) ⊗ F^*(L^⊗3) and its zero-degree components, the fibre contraction, descent of F and of the ample A', uniform generation, vanishing and normal generation, the Veronese relative Proj, flatness, nodality, structure-sheaf identities, retained smooth disjoint sections, the excluded numerical types, stability of the result, base change and coherence of repeated forgetting

targets.target: Blichfeldt's theorem for measurable sets
targets.note: Stated for any countable group acting measurably with an invariant measure and a fundamental domain F: if mu F < mu s for null-measurable s, two distinct translates of s meet. The lattice-point form (a nonzero difference in s - s) is not a separate named lemma.

targets.target: Minkowski's first (convex body) theorem, strict and boundary (compact, non-strict) versions
targets.note: Strict version: convex symmetric s, a countable subgroup L of E with fundamental domain F for an additive Haar measure, mu F * 2^n < mu s (no measurability assumption needed). Boundary version: s also compact, L discrete, E nontrivial, with <=. Non-full-rank lattices are excluded only through the fundamental-domain volume hypothesis; dimension zero is vacuous in the strict version and excluded by [Nontrivial E] in the non-strict one.

targets.target: Discriminants of quadratic forms (square-class invariant, compatibility with sums and localization)
targets.note: Discriminant and signed discriminant in K^x/(K^x)^2 on isometry classes (char not 2), with orthogonal-sum and tensor formulas, base change, and localization at finite, real and complex places of a number field. targets.target: Clifford and Hasse(-Witt) invariants of quadratic forms in Br_2(K)
targets.note: Ingredients only: Clifford algebras (Mathlib), the Brauer group of a field as a commutative group, quaternion norm forms and splitting/Steinberg symbol relations (Tau Ceti; centrality is proved only for Hamilton quaternions). There is no quaternion symbol class (a,b) in Br(K), no Hasse or Hasse-Witt invariant and no Clifford invariant of a form.

targets.target: Local classification of quadratic forms (real, complex, nonarchimedean including dyadic)
targets.note: Real forms are classified by signature (Sylvester in Mathlib, the classification theorem in Tau Ceti) and forms over algebraically closed fields by dimension.
